method.description: A colorimetric measurement of esterase activity where the rate of hydrolysis of acetylcholine with hydroxylamine to form hydroxamic acid is measured to determine acetylcholine levels.

evidence.source-text: Hestrin’s method involves a colorimetric measurement of esterase activity. The rate of hydrolysis of acetylcholine with hydroxylamine to form hydroxamic acid is measured to determine the amount of acetylcholine: RCOOR’ + H2NOH -> RCONHOH + R’OH
This method is performed at alkaline pH in water and is applicable over a wide range of ester concentrations (Hestrin 1949).

method.description: High-pressure liquid chromatography coupled to electrochemical detection, based on enzymatic conversion of acetylcholine into choline and acetate by acetylcholinesterase, and subsequent oxidation of choline to betaine and hydrogen peroxide for detection.

evidence.source-text: High-pressure liquid chromatography coupled to electrochemical detection (HPLC-EC) is based on enzymatic conversion of acetylcholine into choline and acetate by acetylcholinesterase, and subsequent oxidation of choline by choline oxidase to betaine and hydrogen peroxide, which can be oxidized on a platinum electrode. This method permits detection of dialysate acetylcholine concentrations in the 5-10 nM range (Zapata, 2009).

evidence.source-text: Direct measures of AChE activity levels can be made using the modified Ellman method, although selective inhibitors that remove other cholinesterases not directly related to cholinergic responses (e.g., butyrylcholinesterase) are required [45,46].
For measuring AChE levels, the Ellman method is recommended with some modifications (Ellman et al., 1961; Wilson et al., 1996)

method.description: Measures the expression levels of AHR/ARNT pathway-dependent genes, such as VEGF, to assess disruption in ARNT-dependent cellular functions.

evidence.source-text: Sustained AHR/ARNT dimerization induced by DLCs may sequester ARNT from its other dimerization partners at inappropriate times during embryonic cardiomorphogenesis, disrupting ARNT-dependent cellular functions

Dimerization between ARNT and HIF-1α forms a transcription factor complex (HIF-1) that binds to hypoxia response enhancer sequences on DNA to activate the expression of genes such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), which is involved in angiogenesis

method.description: Chromatin immunoprecipitation measures the interaction of proteins with specific genomic regions in vivo by crosslinking proteins and DNA, immunoprecipitation with an antibody, and DNA sequencing.

evidence.source-text: Chromatin immunoprecipitation measures the interaction of proteins with specific genomic regions in vivo [28].
It involves the treatment of cells with formaldehyde to crosslink neighboring protein-protein and protein-DNA molecules [28].
Enrichment of specific DNA sequences represents regions on the genome that the protein of interest is associated with in vivo [28].

method.description: This assay measures the interaction of the AHR complex with specific genomic regions in vivo by crosslinking, shearing DNA, and immunoprecipitating with an antibody against the AHR.

evidence.source-text: Chromatin immunoprecipitation measures the interaction of proteins with specific genomic regions in vivo. It involves the treatment of cells with formaldehyde to crosslink neighboring protein-protein and protein-DNA molecules. Nuclear fractions are isolated, the genomic DNA is sheared, and nuclear lysates are used in immunoprecipitations with an antibody against the protein of interest. After reversal of the crosslinking, the associated DNA fragments are sequenced. Enrichment of specific DNA sequences represents regions on the genome that the protein of interest is associated with in vivo.

method.description: This assay measures the binding of the AHR complex to DNA in vitro by detecting the slower migration of protein-DNA complexes through a polyacrylamide gel.

evidence.source-text: Electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) provides a rapid method to study DNA-binding protein interactions in vitro. This relies on the fact that complexes of protein and DNA migrate through a nondenaturing polyacrylamide gel more slowly than free DNA fragments. The protein-DNA complex components are then identified with appropriate antibodies.

method.description: An in vitro assay used to study DNA-binding protein interactions by migrating protein-DNA complexes through a polyacrylamide gel.

evidence.source-text: Electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) provides a rapid method to study DNA-binding protein interactions in vitro
The EMSA assay was found to be consistent with the LRG assay in chicken hepatoma cells dosed with dioxin-like compounds

method.description: Uses in vitro transcription/translation to synthesize AHR protein, incubated with radiolabeled TDCPP and a HAP pellet; radioactivity is measured to determine saturation or competitive binding.

evidence.source-text: The HAP binding assay makes use of an in vitro transcription/translation method to synthesize the AHR protein, which is then incubated with radiolabeled TDCPP and a HAP pellet.
The occupied protein adsorbs to the HAP and the radioactivity is measured to determine saturation binding.
This assay is simple, repeatable and reproducible; however, it is insensitive to weak ligand-receptor interactions

method.description: The HAP binding assay uses an in vitro transcription/translation method to synthesize AHR protein, which is incubated with radiolabeled TDCPP and a HAP pellet to measure saturation binding.

method.description: This assay measures the binding affinity of ligands to the AHR by synthesizing the AHR protein in vitro, incubating it with radiolabeled ligands, and using hydroxyapatite to separate bound from unbound ligand.

evidence.source-text: The HAP binding assay makes use of an in vitro transcription/translation method to synthesize the AHR protein, which is then incubated with radiolabeled TDCPP and a HAP pellet. The occupied protein adsorbs to the HAP and the radioactivity is measured to determine saturation binding. An additional ligand can also be included in the mixture in order to determine its binding affinity relative to TCDD (competitive binding).

method.description: In silico homology modeling of the ligand binding domain of the AHR, combined with molecular docking simulations, provides insight into the transactivation-potential of AHR ligands.

evidence.source-text: In silico homology modeling of the ligand binding domain of the AHR in combination with molecular docking simulations can provide valuable insight into the transactivation-potential of a diverse array of AHR ligands.

Such models have been developed for multiple AHR isoforms and ligands (high/low affinity, endogenous and synthetic, agonists and antagonists), and can accurately predict ligand potency based on their structure and physicochemical properties.
Bonati et al 2017; Hirano et al 2015; Sovadinova et al 2006

method.description: This assay measures AHR activation by transfecting cells with an AHR clone and a luciferase reporter construct, then exposing them to test compounds and measuring luminescence as a proxy for AHR activation.

evidence.source-text: A monkey kidney cell line (Cos-7) that has low endogenous AHR1 expression was transfected with the appropriate avian AHR1 clone, cormorant ARNT1, a CYP1A5 firefly luciferase reporter construct and a Renilla luciferase vector to control for transfection efficiency. After seeding, the cells were exposed to DLC and luciferase activity was measured using a luminometer. Luminescence, which is proportional to the extent of AHR activation, is expressed as the ratio of firefly luciferase units to Renilla luciferase units.

method.description: A method for evaluating nuclear receptor activation where AHR cDNAs are cloned into an expression vector with a reporter gene (e.g., luciferase, P-lactamase, or CAT) and transfected into recipient cells.

evidence.source-text: Transient transfection transactivation is the most common method for evaluating nuclear receptor activation

evidence.source-text: Dold and Greenlee developed a method to detect specific binding of TCDD to whole mammalian cells in culture and was later modified by Farmahin et al. for avian species. The cultured cells are incubated with radiolabeled TCDD with or without the presence of a competing ligand and filtered. The occupied protein adsorbs onto the filter and the radioactivity is measured to determine saturation binging and/or competitive binding.

evidence.source-text: In medaka, development of papillary processes, which normally only appear on the second to seventh or eighth fin aray of the anal fin, has also been used as an indirect measure of androgen receptor agonism (OECD 2012).

method.description: In vivo measurement of phenotypic masculinization in female fish as an indirect measure of androgen receptor agonism.

evidence.source-text: In fish, phenotypic masculinization of females has frequently been used as an indirect measurement of in vivo androgen receptor agonism.

Development of nuptial tubercles, a dorsal fatpad, and a characteristic banding pattern has been observed in female fathead minnows exposed to androgen agonists (Ankley et al. 2003; Jensen et al. 2006; Ankley et al. 2010; LaLone et al. 2013; OECD 2012).
Anal fin elongation in female western mosquitofish (Gambusia affinis) has similarly been viewed as evidence of AR activation (Raut et al. 2011; Sone et al. 2005).

In medaka, development of papillary processes, which normally only appear on the second to seventh or eighth fin aray of the anal fin, has also been used as an indirect measure of androgen receptor agonism (OECD 2012).

evidence.source-text: Aortic explants cultured from developing chick embryos or mouse/rat fetuses have been used as a source for evaluating drug/chemical effects on microvessel outgrowth [Baker et al. 2011; Beedie et al. 2015; Ellis-Hutchings et al. 2017; Kapoor et al. 2020; Katakia et al. 2020]. method.description: Uses induced pluripotent stem cell-derived endothelial cells (iPSC-EC) cultured in 3D hydrogel microspheres or microfluidic devices to evaluate VEGF-dependent vascular network formation and sprouting behaviors.
method.measured-endpoint: vascular network formation and sprouting behaviors

evidence.source-text: Engineered microtissues: To better recapitulate angiogenesis in vivo, in vitro assays for drug and chemical screening must adopt physiological relevant culture conditions with robustness and scalability. Human endothelial lines have been derived from induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC-EC) and cultured in engineered platforms that mimic the 3D microenvironment [Belair et al. 2015]. They formed VEGF-dependent 3D perfusable vascular networks when co-cultured with fibroblasts and aligned with flow in microfluidic devices [Belair et al. 2015]. Encapsulating endothelial cells at controlled densities in hydrogel microspheres surrounded by a synthetic ECM [Belair et al. 2016a] or VEGF-binding peptides [Belair et al. 2016b] can be used to evaluate the activation by ECM and ECM-sequestered VEGF and other angiogenic factors.

method.description: Uses human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) co-cultured with fibroblasts to form endothelial networks resembling a microvascular bed upon VEGF stimulation, quantified by immunochemical biomarkers and image analysis.
method.guideline: OECD Guidance Document 34 for the Validation and International Acceptance of New or Updated Test Methods for Hazard Assessment

evidence.source-text: Human cell-based in vitro tubulogenesis assay: Angiogenic sprouts convert into endothelial tubules and form connections with other vessels, which requires the local suppression of motility and the formation of new cell-cell junctions. In vitro assays for this assembly, commonly referred to as tubulogenesis, use human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) co-cultured with fibroblasts [Bishop et al. 1999]. Routine cell culture methods support the organization of isolated HUVEC cells into endothelial networks that resemble a microvascular bed upon stimulation with VEGF. The standardized assay detects pro-angiogenic and anti-angiogenic activities that are tracked with with immunochemical biomarkers (eg, PECAM-1) and quantified by image analysis [Bishop et al. 1999].

method.assay-name: In silico computational modeling of angiogenesis
method.description: Mathematical and computational models simulate angiogenic sprouting, including molecular control of tip/stalk switching dynamics linked to VEGF-Notch-DLL4 signaling, EC-tip and EC-stalk differentiation, and tubulogenesis for predictive toxicology.
method.measured-endpoint: angiogenic sprouting dynamics, tip/stalk switching and tubulogenesis simulation

evidence.source-text: in silico computational models for quantitative simulation and biological integration.

These aspects of angiogenic sprouting have been modelled in silico mathematically or computationally, probing deeply into the molecular control of tip/stalk switching dynamics linked to the VEGF-Notch-DLL4 signaling [Venkataraman et al. 2016], uncovering the critical determinants of EC-tip and EC-stalk differentiation that influence the morphology of sprout progression [Palm et al. 2016], establishing canonical growth trajectories in normal and chemical-disrupted zebrafish embryos [Shirinifard et al. 2013], and simulating cell-cell interactions in a self-organizing computer model of tubulogenesis for predictive toxicology [Kleinstreuer et al. 2013].

evidence.source-text: A vascular sprouting assay that utilizes mouse embryonic stem cells differentiated into vascularized embryoid bodies has been described, where the microsystem cultured onto 3D-collagen gels recapitulates key features of in vivo sprouting including endothelial EC-tip cell selection, migration and proliferation, polarized guidance, tubulogenesis, and mural cell recruitment

method.description: Aromatase activity is measured by evaluating the production of tritiated water released upon the aromatase catalyzed conversion of radio-labeled androstenedione to estrone.

evidence.source-text: Aromatase activity is typically measured by evaluating the production of tritiated water released upon the aromatase catalyzed conversion of radio-labeled androstenedione to estrone (Lephart and Simpson 1991).

Aromatase activity can be measured in cell lines exposed in vitro (e.g., human placental JEG-3 cells and JAR choriocarcinoma cells, (Letcher et al. 1999); H295R human adrenocortical carcinoma cells (Sanderson et al. 2000)).
OECD Test Guideline No. 456 H295R Steroidogenesis Assay can be used to indirectly assess aromatase activity by measuring estradiol production by the H295R cells (OECD, 2013).

ontology-term.label: cysteine-type endopeptidase activity involved in apoptotic process

evidence.source-text: Caspase activity assays measured by fluorescence. During apoptosis, mainly caspase-3 and -7 cleave PARP to yield an 85 kDa and a 25 kDa fragment. PARP cleavage is considered to be one of the classical characteristics of apoptosis. Antibodies to the 85 kDa fragment of cleaved PARP or to caspase-3 both serve as markers for apoptotic cells that can be monitored using immunofluorescence (Li, Peng et al., 2004).

method.description: A fluorescent assay that stains condensed or fragmented DNA in live or fixed cells, serving as a marker of apoptosis.

evidence.source-text: Hoechst 33342 staining: Hoechst dyes are cell-permeable and bind to DNA in live or fixed cells. Therefore, these stains are often called supravital, which means that cells survive a treatment with these compounds. The stained, condensed or fragmented DNA is a marker of apoptosis (Loo, 2002; Kubbies and Rabinovitch, 1983).

method.description: Measures the release of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) into cell culture medium as an indicator of plasma membrane damage and necrosis. LDH catalyzes the oxidation of lactate to pyruvate, producing NADH, which then reduces a tetrazolium salt to a colored formazan product quantified by spectroscopy.

evidence.source-text: Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) is a soluble cytoplasmic enzyme that is present in almost all cells and is released into extracellular space when the plasma membrane is damaged. To detect the leakage of LDH into cell culture medium, a tetrazolium salt is used in this assay.

The amount of formazan product can be colorimetrically quantified by standard spectroscopy. Because of the linearity of the assay, it can be used to enumerate the percentage of necrotic cells in a sample (Chan et al., 2013).

method.description: Measures the release of the soluble cytoplasmic enzyme lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) into the extracellular space due to plasma membrane damage using a tetrazolium salt colorimetric method.

method.description: A colorimetric assay that measures cell viability by quantifying the reduction of the tetrazolium dye MTT to insoluble formazan by NAD(P)H-dependent cellular oxidoreductase enzymes.

evidence.source-text: The MTT assay is a colorimetric assay for assessing cell viability. NAD(P)H-dependent cellular oxidoreductase enzymes may reflect the number of viable cells present.

Tetrazolium dye assays can also be used to measure cytotoxicity (loss of viable cells) or cytostatic activity (shift from proliferation to quiescence) of potential medicinal agents and toxic materials.

method.description: The MTT assay is a colorimetric assay that assesses cell viability by measuring the reduction of MTT dye to formazan by NAD(P)H-dependent cellular oxidoreductase enzymes. It can also measure cytotoxicity or cytostatic activity.

evidence.source-text: The MTT assay is a colorimetric assay for assessing cell viability.

Tetrazolium dye assays can also be used to measure cytotoxicity or cytostatic activity (loss of viable cells) or cytostatic activity (shift from proliferation to quiescence) of potential medicinal agents and toxic materials.
MTT assays are usually done in the dark since the MTT reagent is sensitive to light (Berridgeet al.,2005).

evidence.source-text: In rodent testes, studies have detected adducts in situ by immuhistocytological staining. For example, fixed testes are incubated with O6-EtGua -specific mouse monoclonal antibody and subsequently with a labeled anti-mouse IgG F antibody. Nuclear DNA is counterstained with DAPI 4,6-diamidino- 2-phenylindole. Fluorescence signals from immunostained O6-EtGua residues in DNA are visualized by fluorescence microscopy and quantitated using an image analysis system. Methods are described in (Seiler et al. 1997).

evidence.source-text: DNA alkylation can also be measured using a modified comet assay. This method involves the digestion of alkylated DNA bases with 3–methyladenine DNA glycosylase (Collins et al., 2001; Hasplova et al., 2012) followed by the standard comet assay to detect where alkyl adducts occur. The advantage of this method is that the alkaline version of the comet assay, as a core method, has an in vivo OECD guideline.

method.description: Rodents are exposed to radio-labeled alkylating agents, and DNA adduct formation is determined after neutral and acid hydrolysis of DNA followed by separation of the various ethylation products using HPLC.

evidence.source-text: Alternatively, rodents have also been exposed to radio-labeled alkylating agents. Examples from the literature include [2-3H] ENU, [1-3H]di-ethyl sulfate, or [1-3H]ethyl-methane sulfonate. Following treatment with the labeled chemical, testis and other tissues of interest are removed. Germ cells are released from tubuli by pushing out the contents with forceps. Using this procedure all germ-cell stages are liberated from the tubuli, with the possible exception of part of the population of stem-cell spermatogonia that remain attached to the walls of the tubuli. DNA is then extracted from germ cells, empty testis tubuli and other tissues of interest. DNA adduct formation is determined after neutral and acid hydrolysis of DNA followed by separation of the various ethylation products using HPLC (described in van Zeeland et al. 1990).

method.description: Measures the enzymatic activities of mitochondrial complexes I to IV using dual wavelength spectrophotometry.

evidence.source-text: Enzymatic activities of the complexes I to IV were determined by dual wavelength spectrophotometry with an Aminco Dual Wavelength 2 ATM UV-VIS spectrophotometer.
Complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) activity was determined at 340 nm with 380 nm as reference wavelength.
Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase) activity was determined by the difference in absorbency between 270 and 330 nm.
Complex III (Ubiquinol-cytochrome c reductase) activity was determined by the difference in absorbency between 550 and 580 nm.
Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase) activity was determined by the difference in absorbency between 550 and 580 nm.

method.description: Measures mitochondrial calcium influx using aequorin as a calcium sensor in conjunction with GFP for bioluminescence resonance energy transfer (BRET).

evidence.source-text: Together with GFP, the aequorin moiety acts as Ca2+ sensor in vivo, which delivers emission energy to the GFP acceptor molecule in a BRET (Bioluminescence Resonance Energy Transfer) process; the Ca2+ can then be visualized with fluorescence microscopy.

method.description: Measures ATP levels using commercially available kits based on luciferin and luciferase activity, or via electrodes or luminometric methods for isolated mitochondria.

evidence.source-text: For the evaluation of ATP levels, various commercially-available ATP assay kits are offered based on luciferin and luciferase activity.

method.description: Measures the levels of reduced (GSH) and oxidized (GSSG) glutathione, often using DTNB (Ellman’s reagent), to assess the cellular redox potential.

evidence.source-text: GSH is regenerated from its oxidized form (GSSH) by the action of an NADPH dependent reductase (GSSH + NADPH + H+ à 2 GSH + NADP+). The ratio of GSH/GSSG is therefore a good indicator for the cellular NADH+/NADPH ratio (i.e. the redox potential).
GSH and GSSH levels can be determined by HPLC, capillary electrophoresis, or biochemically with DTNB (Ellman’s reagent).

method.description: Measures the oxygen consumption rate in cells or isolated mitochondria, often combined with other endpoints to derive specific information on mitochondrial function.

evidence.source-text: Cellular oxygen consumption.
The oxygen consumption parameter can be combined with other endpoints to derive more specific information on the efficacy of mitochondrial function.

method.description: Measures the activity of the mitochondrial electron transport system using a cell-free homogenate incubated with NADH and an artificial electron acceptor (INT).

ontology-term.label: mitochondrial electron transport, NADH to ubiquinone

evidence.source-text: Determination of ETS activity can be dene following Owens and King's assay (1975). The technique is based on a cell-free homogenate that is incubated with NADH to saturate the mitochondrial ETS and an artificial electron acceptor [l - (4 -iodophenyl) -3 - (4 -nitrophenyl) -5-phenylte trazolium chloride (INT)] to register the electron transmission rate.

process.label: mitochondrial electron transport, NADH to ubiquinone

method.description: Determines electron transport system activity in cell-free homogenates by incubating with NADH and an artificial electron acceptor (INT), measuring INT-formazan production spectrophotometrically.

evidence.source-text: The technique is based on a cell-free homogenate that is incubated with NADH to saturate the mitochondrial ETS and an artificial electron acceptor [l - (4 -iodophenyl) -3 - (4 -nitrophenyl) -5-phenylte trazolium chloride (INT)] to register the electron transmission rate. The oxygen consumption rate is calculated from the molar production rate of INT-formazan which is determined spectrophotometrically

The method is based on the detection of OCR (Oxygen Consumption Rate) that represents mitochondrial respiration as well as on the detection of ECAR (extracellular acidification rate) / proton efflux rate (PER): reflects extracellular acidification, a proxy for glycolysis (lactate release) plus contributions from CO₂/HCO₃⁻.

method.description: Combines R123 fluorescence (for mitochondrial membrane potential) and propidium iodide (for cell viability) using a flow cytometer.

evidence.source-text: Dc and viability were determined by analyzing the R123 and propidium iodide fluorescence intensity with a FACScan flow cytometer

R123 is a cationic dye that accumulates in the negatively charged inner side of the mitochondria. When the potential drops, less R123 accumulates in the mitochondria, which results in a lower fluorescence signal.

method.description: Detects hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production using fluorogenic substrates (diacetyldichlorofluorescein, homovanillic acid, Amplex® Red) in conjunction with horseradish peroxidase (HRP). Increasing amounts of H2O2 produce increasing fluorescent product.

evidence.source-text: e. Detection of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. There are a number of fluorogenic substrates, which serve as hydrogen donors that have been used in conjunction with horseradish peroxidase (HRP) enzyme to produce intensely fluorescent products in the presence of hydrogen peroxide (Zhou et al., 1997: Ruch et al., 1983). The more commonly used substrates include diacetyldichloro-fluorescein, homovanillic acid, and Amplex® Red. In these examples, increasing amounts of H2O2 form increasing amounts of fluorescent product (Tarpley et al., 2004).

method.description: Measures the formation of thiobarbituric acid-reactive substances (TBARS), such as malondialdehyde, as an indicator of lipid peroxidation.

evidence.source-text: Measurement of lipid peroxidation has historically relied on the detection of thiobarbituric acid (TBA)-reactive compounds such as malondialdehyde generated from the decomposition of cellular membrane lipid under oxidative stress (Pryor et al., 1976).

method.description: Uses fluorescent probes like TMRE or TMRM to measure the mitochondrial membrane potential in living cells, with detection via flow cytometry, microscopy, or plate readers.

evidence.source-text: Quantitative assessment of ΔΨm in living cells is most commonly achieved through the use of cationic, lipophilic fluorescent probes that accumulate within the mitochondrial matrix in proportion to the electrochemical gradient (Leonard et al., 2014).

Among these, tetramethylrhodamine derivatives such as TMRE (tetramethylrhodamine ethyl ester) and TMRM (tetramethylrhodamine methyl ester) are widely employed due to their reversible, potential-dependent distribution across the inner mitochondrial membrane (Scaduto and Grotyohann, 1999; Creed and McKenzie, 2019).

method.assay-name: Mitochondrial permeability transition pore (PTP) opening assay
method.description: Detects PTP opening through the translocation of cytochrome c, adenylate kinase, or AIF, or via calcein fluorescence quenching in permeabilized cells.

evidence.source-text: The opening of the PTP is associated with a permeabilization of mitochondrial membranes, so that different compounds and cellular constituents can change intracellular localization. This can be measured by assessment of the translocation of cytochrome c, adenylate kinase or AIF from mitochondria to the cytosol or nucleus.

method.assay-name: Mitochondrial permeability transition pore (PTP) opening assay
method.description: Measures the opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore by assessing the translocation of cytochrome c, adenylate kinase, or AIF, or using a calcein fluorescence quenching assay.

evidence.source-text: The opening of the PTP is associated with a permeabilization of mitochondrial membranes, so that different compounds and cellular constituents can change intracellular localization. This can be measured by assessment of the translocation of cytochrome c, adenylate kinase or AIF from mitochondria to the cytosol or nucleus.
An alternative approach is to measure the accessibility of cobalt to the mitochondrial matrix in a calcein fluorescence quenching assay in live permeabilized cells (Petronilli et al., 1999).

method.description: Measures the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) such as superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals using direct or indirect assays.

evidence.source-text: Electrons from the mitochondrial ETS may be transferred ‘erroneously’ to molecular oxygen to form superoxide anions. This type of side reaction can be strongly enhanced upon mitochondrial damage.

As superoxide may form hydrogen peroxide, hydroxyl radicals or other reactive oxygen species, a large number of direct ROS assays and assays assessing the effects of ROS (indirect ROS assays) are available (Adam-Vizi, 2005; Fan and Li 2014).

evidence.source-text: A variety of in vitro mammalian cell gene mutation tests are described in OECD’s Test Guidelines 476 (2016) and 490 (2015).

TG 476 (2016) is used to identify substances that induce gene mutations at the hprt (hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyl transferase) gene, or the transgenic xprt (xanthine-guanine phosphoribosyl transferase) reporter locus.

method.description: A bacterial reverse mutation test used to determine if a chemical can cause gene mutations by analyzing the growth capacity of different bacterial strains in the presence and absence of metabolic activation systems.

evidence.source-text: The Salmonella mutagenicity test (Ames Test) is generally used as part of a first tier screen to determine if a chemical can cause gene mutations.

A variety of bacterial strains are used, in the presence and absence of a metabolic activation system (e.g., rat liver microsomal S9 fraction), to determine the mutagenic potency of chemicals by dose-response analysis.

method.description: Measures electrical activity in cultured neurons in response to NMDA receptor activation or inactivation.

evidence.source-text: Microelectrode array (MEA) recordings are used to measure electrical activity in cultured neurons in response to NMDA receptor activation or inactivation.
MEAs can also be applied in higher throughput platforms to facilitate screening of numerous chemical compounds based on electrical activity measurements.

method.description: Measures the activation or inhibition of NMDA receptors by recording ion channels selective to Na+, K+, and Ca2+ in neuronal cells.

evidence.source-text: The measurement of the activation or the inhibition of NMDA receptors is done indirectly by recording the individual ion channels that are selective to Na+, K+ and Ca+2 by the patch clamp technique.

The whole-cell patch clamp recording techniques have also been used to study synaptically-evoked NMDA receptor-mediated excitatory or inhibitory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs and IPSCs, respectively) in brain slices and neuronal cells, allowing the evaluation of the activated or inhibited state of the receptor.

method.description: Whole-cell patch clamp recording techniques are used to study synaptically-evoked NMDA receptor-mediated excitatory or inhibitory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs and IPSCs) in brain slices and neuronal cells, evaluating the activated or inhibited state of the receptor.

evidence.source-text: The whole-cell patch clamp recording techniques have also been used to study synaptically-evoked NMDA receptor-mediated excitatory or inhibitory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs and IPSCs, respectively) in brain slices and neuronal cells, allowing the evaluation of the activated or inhibited state of the receptor (Ogdon and Stanfield, 2009; Zhao et al., 2009).

method.description: Measures NMDA receptor ion channel activity by recording ionic currents (e.g., EPSCs/IPSCs) through selective Na+, K+, Ca2+ channels using the patch clamp technique, assessing channel open/closed states.

This method relies on lack of measurable ion flux when NMDA ion channel is closed, whereas constant channel specific conductance is recorded at the open state of the receptor

evidence.source-text: Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI) is a soft ionization technique used in mass spectrometry, allowing the analysis of biomolecules (biopolymers such as DNA, proteins, peptides and sugars) and large organic molecules (such as polymers, dendrimers and other macromolecules), which tend to be fragile and fragment when ionized by more conventional ionization methods.

MALDI methodology is a three-step process. First, the sample is mixed with a suitable matrix material and applied to a metal plate. Second, a pulsed laser irradiates the sample, triggering ablation and desorption of the sample and matrix material. Finally, the analyte molecules are ionized by being protonated or deprotonated in the hot plume of ablated gases, and can then be accelerated into whichever mass spectrometer is used to analyse them.

method.description: This assay involves fixing, dehydrating, and embedding tissues in wax, cutting sections to 3–5 μm thickness, staining, and examining under a microscope to identify tissue changes.

evidence.source-text: Histopathology focuses on the changes in tissues and is a technique used for identifying correlations with biochemical markers. Generally renal pathology is measured after either whole organism or specific tissue of interest is fixed, dehydrated, and then embedded in wax, commonly paraffin wax. Sections are then cut to approximately 3–5 μm in thickness and stained before being examined under a microscope (e.g., Folmar et al., 2001; Mihaich et al., 2012; Zha et al., 2007).

method.description: Histopathology examines tissue changes after fixation, dehydration, embedding, sectioning, and staining, then microscopic examination to identify correlations with biochemical markers. It is used to measure renal pathology.

Generally renal pathology is measured after either whole organism or specific tissue of interest is fixed, dehydrated, and then embedded in wax, commonly paraffin wax.
Sections are then cut to approximately 3–5 μm in thickness and stained before being examined under a microscope (e.g., Folmar et al., 2001; Mihaich et al., 2012; Zha et al., 2007).

method.description: Predicts vascular insufficiency for potential vascular disrupting chemicals using pathway analysis.

evidence.source-text: Computational models: Critical pathways for developmental angiogenesis and potential disruptions have critical signal-response systems embedded in three types of receptors that play key roles in a number of morphoregulatory processes: receptor tyrosine kinases (e.g., growth factor-signaling), G-protein coupled receptors (e.g., chemokine signaling), and GPI-anchored receptors (e.g., uPAR system). Computational approaches have been used to predict vascular insufficiency for potential vascular disrupting chemicals (pVDCs) that are developmental toxicants or non-toxicants [Kleinstreuer et al. 2011; Knudsen and Kleinstreuer, 2011]. This has been applied to the ToxCast inventory to rank order over a thousand chemicals for validation testing [McCollum et al. 2017; Tal et al. 2017; Saili et al. 2019; Zurlinden et al. 2020].

method.description: A quantitative imaging assay using live-cell and confocal microscopy to detect trajectory dynamics and subtle morphological changes in vascular patterning in zebrafish embryos during chemical exposure.

evidence.source-text: Live-cell imaging has been used to quantitatively detect the trajectory dynamics of vascular patterning [Clendenon et al. 2013; Shirinfard et al. 2013] and confocal cell imaging has been used to develop a quantitative assay capable of detecting relatively subtle changes (~8%) in relative to controls during chemical exposure [Tal et al. 2017].

method.description: A functional assay using cultured rat aortic tissue explants to evaluate angiogenesis and vascular development in response to chemical exposure.

evidence.source-text: Complex functional assays such as the rat aortic explant assay, rat whole embryo culture, and the zebrafish embryotoxicity along with transcriptomic signatures provide a tiered approach to evaluate HTS signatures and their taxonomic implications for conserved pathways to prioritize further in vivo testing studies [Ellis-Hutchings et al. 2017].
anchored the results to complex in vitro functional assays: the rat aortic explant assay, rat whole embryo culture, and zebrafish embryotoxicity [Saili et al. 2019].

evidence.source-text: Zebrafish reporter assays: Blood flow begins in the zebrafish embryo at ∼24 h postfertilization. Shortly after this, the angiogenic vessels that perfuse the trunk of the embryo (intersegmental vessels) sprout from the vasculogenic vessels [Tran et al. 2007]. These effects can be visualized in automated, quantitative screening assays using transgenic zebrafish expressing green fluorescent protein (GFP) under the control of the vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR) Vegfr2 promoter that restricts reporter gene expression to developing blood vessels.

Complex functional assays such as the rat aortic explant assay, rat whole embryo culture, and the zebrafish embryotoxicity along with transcriptomic signatures provide a tiered approach to evaluate HTS signatures and their taxonomic implications for conserved pathways to prioritize further in vivo testing studies [Ellis-Hutchings et al. 2017].

ToxCast: A study evaluated two anti-angiogenic agents, 5HPP-33, a synthetic Thalidomide analog [Noguchi et al. 2005] and TNP-470, a synthetic Fumagillan analog [Ingber et al. 1990] across the ToxCast HTS assay platform and anchored the results to complex in vitro functional assays: the rat aortic explant assay, rat whole embryo culture, and zebrafish embryotoxicity [Saili et al. 2019]. Both compounds disrupted angiogenesis and embryogenesis in the functional assays, with differences in potency and adverse effects.

method.description: Uses transgenic zebrafish with GFP under VEGFR promoter to visualize and quantify vascular development.

evidence.source-text: Zebrafish reporter assays: Blood flow begins in the zebrafish embryo at ∼24 h postfertilization. Shortly after this, the angiogenic vessels that perfuse the trunk of the embryo (intersegmental vessels) sprout from the vasculogenic vessels [Tran et al. 2007]. These effects can be visualized in automated, quantitative screening assays using transgenic zebrafish expressing green fluorescent protein (GFP) under the control of the vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR) Vegfr2 promoter that restricts reporter gene expression to developing blood vessels. Phenotypic readouts have been used to screen and validate anti-angiogenic compounds [Tran et al. 2007; Yano et al. 2012; Yozzo et al. 2013; Tal et al. 2014; McCollum et al. 2017]. Live-cell imaging has been used to quantitatively detect the trajectory dynamics of vascular patterning [Clendenon et al. 2013; Shirinfard et al. 2013] and confocal cell imaging has been used to develop a quantitative assay capable of detecting relatively subtle changes (~8%) in relative to controls during chemical exposure [Tal et al. 2017].

the stages are determined by both the quantity and location of the fibrosis, with the formation of septa and nodules as major factors in the transition from one stage to the next

method.description: This assay measures the levels of matrix metalloproteinases 2 and 3 (MMP-2, MMP-3) and tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases 1 and 2 (TIMP-1, TIMP-2), direct markers of fibrosis associated with matrix degradation.

evidence.source-text: Other direct markers of fibrosis are those associated with matrix degradation, ie, matrix metalloproteinases 2 and 3 (MMP-2, MMP- 3) and tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases 1 and 2 (TIMP-1, TIMP-2).

method.description: This assay measures the levels of procollagen type III amino-terminal peptide (P3NP) in serum, a direct serologic marker of hepatic fibrosis associated with matrix deposition.

evidence.source-text: Direct serologic markers of fibrosis include those associated with matrix deposition — e.g.procollagen type III amino-terminal peptide (P3NP), type I and IV collagens, laminin, hyaluronic acid, and chondrex.
P3NP is the most widely studied marker of hepatic fibrosis.

method.description: Measurement of direct biochemical markers in serum associated with matrix deposition (e.g., P3NP, collagens, laminin) or matrix degradation (e.g., MMPs, TIMPs).

evidence.source-text: Direct serologic markers of fibrosis include those associated with matrix deposition — e.g.procollagen type III amino-terminal peptide (P3NP), type I and IV collagens, laminin, hyaluronic acid, and chondrex.

Other direct markers of fibrosis are those associated with matrix degradation, ie, matrix metalloproteinases 2 and 3 (MMP-2, MMP- 3) and tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases 1 and 2 (TIMP-1, TIMP-2).

method.description: Measurement of the distance from the anus to the genitals as a biomarker of prenatal androgen exposure and reproductive health risks.

evidence.source-text: The anogenital distance (AGD) is a sexual dimorphism that results from the sex difference in foetal androgen (DHT) levels (Rhees et al., 1997).
Measurement of AGD has also been proposed as a quantitative biomarker of foetal endocrine disruptor exposure in humans (Arbuckle et al. 2008), (Dean and Sharpe 2013).
Decreased AGD in male rats is a hallmark of exposure to antiandrogenic substances (Noriega et al, 2009; Christiansen et al, 2010).

The extended one-generation in vivo reproductive toxicity study OECD TG 443 is used to investigate adverse effects of chemical substances on fertility and developmental toxicity in the rat, in which AGD is measured.

method.description: Detection of structural abnormalities or pathological changes in the male reproductive tract through visual inspection.

evidence.source-text: Malformations are detected by macroscopically for any structural abnormality or pathological change.

The Congenital malformation of the genitalia is a medical term referring to a broad category of conditions that for humans is classified by International Classification of Diseases (ICD) in chapter "Congenital malformations of genital organs" (Q50-Q56) e.g.Q54 Hypospadias, Q53 Undescended testicle.

method.description: Macroscopic visual inspection of the male reproductive tract to detect any structural abnormality or pathological change associated with congenital malformations of the genitalia.

evidence.source-text: the OECD 202 Daphnia sp. Acute immobilization test (OECD 2004) which can also be modified depending on the effect one expects.

method.description: A method used in ecology to estimate animal population size by capturing, marking, and recapturing individuals.

evidence.source-text: in the field, for example by determining age structure after one capture, or by capture-mark-recapture efforts. The latter is a method commonly used in ecology to estimate an animal population's size where it is impractical to count every individual.

method.description: Mortality is measured by observing the cessation of heart beat, breathing, and locomotory movements. The metric reported is the mortality rate.

evidence.source-text: Mortality of animals is generally observed as cessation of the heart beat, breathing (gill or lung movement) and locomotory movements.
The reported metric is mostly the mortality rate: the number of deaths in a given area or period, or from a particular cause.

method.description: Fluoro-Jade staining is used to detect degenerating neurons by binding to anionic components of degenerating cells, providing a fluorescent marker for neurodegeneration.

evidence.source-text: Fluoro-Jade, an anionic fluorescent dye, is a good marker of degenerating neurons.
Fluoro-Jade and Fluoro-Jade B were found to stain all degenerating neurons, regardless of specific insult or mechanism of cell death
Fluoro-Jade C was shown to be highly resistant to fading and compatible with virtually all histological processing and staining protocols
Fluoro-Jade C is a good tool for detecting acutely and chronically degenerating neurons

method.description: Uses a modeling framework to link stressor effects on growth, reproduction, and survival to energy acquisition and processing, informing population growth rate estimates.

evidence.source-text: Dynamic energy budget (DEB) models offer a methodology that reverse engineers stressor effects on growth, reproduction, and/or survival into modular characterizations related to the acquisition and processing of energy resources (Nisbet et al. 2000, Nisbet et al. 2011).

method.description: Combines field-based effects monitoring data informed by an AOP with a population model to project declines in population growth rate.

evidence.source-text: A model construct could be based upon a combination of effects-based monitoring at field sites (informed by an AOP) and a population model. Miller et al. (2015) applied a population model informed by an AOP to project declines in population growth rate for white suckers (Catostomus commersoni) using observed changes in sex steroid synthesis in fish exposed to a complex pulp and paper mill effluent in Jackfish Bay, Ontario, Canada.

method.description: Integrates endogenous lifecycle processes of growth, development, survival, and reproduction to estimate fitness and predict effects of chemical stressors on vital rates.

evidence.source-text: ● Endogenous Lifecycle Models (ELMs), capture the endogenous lifecycle processes of growth, development, survival, and reproduction and integrate these to estimate and predict expected fitness (Etterson and Ankley, 2021). AOPs can be used to inform ELMs of effects of chemical stressors on the vital rates that determine fitness, and to decide what hierarchical models of endogenous systems should be included within an ELM (Etterson and Ankley, 2021).

method.assay-name: Laboratory toxicity tests with population modeling
method.description: Combines laboratory toxicity data (e.g., reproductive assays) with population models to estimate declines in population growth rate.

evidence.source-text: A modeling construct could be based upon laboratory toxicity tests to determine effect(s) that are then linked to the population model and used to estimate decline in population growth rate. Miller et al. (2007) used concentration–response data from short term reproductive assays with fathead minnow (Pimephales promelas) exposed to endocrine disrupting chemicals in combination with a population model to examine projected alterations in population growth rate.

method.description: Estimates population size by marking individuals (e.g., tags, bands, transmitters) and recapturing them at a later time to determine population growth rate.

evidence.source-text: For species that are mobile throughout a large range, a strategy such as using a mark-recapture method may be employed (i.e. tags, bands, transmitters) to determine a count over a time interval (at time = 0 and again at time =1).

method.description: Uses mathematical constructs (e.g., differential equations, matrix projection models) to estimate population growth rate based on experimental or field data.

evidence.source-text: Population growth rate can also be estimated using mathematical model constructs (for example, ranging from simple differential equations to complex age or stage structured matrix projection models and individual based modeling approaches), and may assume a linear or nonlinear population increase over time.

method.description: Measures population size by dividing a habitat into units and counting organisms within selected units at two time points to estimate population growth rate.

evidence.source-text: For stationary species an observational strategy may involve dividing a habitat into units. After setting up the units, samples are performed throughout the habitat at a select number of units (determined using a statistical sampling design) over a time interval (at time t = 0 and again at time t = 1), and the total number of organisms within each unit are counted.

method.description: Measures population size at two time points by counting organisms within sampled habitat units to estimate population growth rate over the interval.

evidence.source-text: For stationary species an observational strategy may involve dividing a habitat into units. After setting up the units, samples are performed throughout the habitat at a select number of units (determined using a statistical sampling design) over a time interval (at time t = 0 and again at time t = 1), and the total number of organisms within each unit are counted.

method.description: Population growth rate (instantaneous growth rate) is measured by sampling a population over a time interval and calculating the difference between the initial and final population sizes, divided by the initial size. This can be done using observational strategies for stationary species or mark-recapture methods for mobile species.

evidence.source-text: The population growth rate, r, can be determined by taking the difference (subtracting) between the initial population size, Nt=0 (population size at time t=0), and the population size at the end of the interval, Nt=1 (population size at time t = 1), and then subsequently dividing by the initial population size.

For stationary species an observational strategy may involve dividing a habitat into units. After setting up the units, samples are performed throughout the habitat at a select number of units (determined using a statistical sampling design) over a time interval (at time t = 0 and again at time t = 1), and the total number of organisms within each unit are counted.

For species that are mobile throughout a large range, a strategy such as using a mark-recapture method may be employed (i.e. tags, bands, transmitters) to determine a count over a time interval (at time = 0 and again at time =1).

method.description: Uses a mathematical framework to model dose-response relationships of key events in an AOP to predict population-level impacts, including declines in population growth rate.

evidence.source-text: A quantitative adverse outcome pathway (qAOP) has been defined as a mathematical construct that models the dose–response or response–response relationships of all KERs described in an AOP (Conolly et al. 2017, Perkins et al. 2019). Conolly et al. (2017) developed a qAOP using data generated with the aromatase inhibitor fadrozole as a stressor and then used it to predict potential population‐level impacts (including decline in population growth rate).

method.description: Measuring changes in sex steroid synthesis in fish exposed to effluent to project declines in population growth rate.

evidence.source-text: Miller et al. (2015) applied a population model informed by an AOP to project declines in population growth rate for white suckers (Catostomus commersoni) using observed changes in sex steroid synthesis in fish exposed to a complex pulp and paper mill effluent in Jackfish Bay, Ontario, Canada.

evidence.source-text: The measurement of the activation or the inhibition of NMDA receptors is done indirectly by recording the individual ion channels that are selective to Na+, K+ and Ca2+ by the patch clamp technique.

The whole-cell patch clamp recording techniques have also been used to study synaptically-evoked NMDA receptor-mediated excitatory or inhibitory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs and IPSCs, respectively) in brain slices and neuronal cells, allowing the evaluation of the activated or inhibited state of the receptor.

method.description: Chemicals are incubated with synthetic peptides containing lysine or cysteine, and the depletion of the peptides is quantified, indicating reactivity towards these amino acids.

evidence.source-text: Protocols and Databases: While methionine, histidine, and serine all possess nucleophilic groups that are found in skin proteins, the –SH group of cysteine and the ε-NH2 group of lysine are the most often studied. Soft electrophilic interactions involving the thiol group can be modelled with small molecules. Glutathione (GSH; L-γ-glutamyl-L-cysteinyl-glycine) is the most widely used model nucleophile in soft electrophilic reactivity assays. [...] Recently, OECD adopted the new Test Guideline (TG) No442C: In chemico skin sensitisation – Direct Peptide Reactivity Assay (DPRA). This method quantifies the reactivity of chemicals towards model synthetic peptides containing either lysine or cysteine [15]. The DPRA protocol can be found in the EURL ECVAM Database Service on Alternative Methods to animal experimentation (DB-ALM): Protocol No154 for Direct Peptide Reactivity Assay (DPRA) for skin sensitisation testing [16].

method.description: This test measures the absorption of radioactive iodine by the thyroid gland over 4-6 hours and 24 hours using a gamma scintillation counter. The percentage of uptake at 24 hours is the primary measurement.

evidence.source-text: The radioactive iodine uptake test, or RAIU test, is a type of scan used in the diagnosis of thyroid gland dysfunction
The patient swallows radioactive iodine in the form of capsule or fluid, and its absorption by the thyroid is studied after 4–6 hours and after 24 hours with the aid of a gamma scintillation counter.

The percentage of RAIU 24 hours after the administration of radioiodide is the most useful, since this is the time when the thyroid gland has reached the plateau of isotope accumulation, and because it has been shown that at this time, the best separation between high, normal, and low uptake is obtained.

method.description: A diagnostic scan that measures the thyroid gland's avidity for iodide by quantifying the absorption of swallowed radioactive iodine using a gamma scintillation counter at specific time intervals.

evidence.source-text: The radioactive iodine uptake test, or RAIU test, is a type of scan used in the diagnosis of thyroid gland dysfunction
The patient swallows radioactive iodine in the form of capsule or fluid, and its absorption by the thyroid is studied after 4–6 hours and after 24 hours with the aid of a gamma scintillation counter.
The percentage of RAIU 24 hours after the administration of radioiodide is the most useful
The test does not measure hormone production and release but merely the avidity of the thyroid gland for iodide and its rate of clearance relative to the kidney.

method.description: Measures cardio-respiratory function in fish by monitoring ventilation rate, cough response, ventilation volume, oxygen consumption, and oxygen utilization.
method.measured-endpoint: ventilation rate, cough response, ventilation volume, oxygen consumption, oxygen utilization

evidence.source-text: Measurements of cardio-respiratory function in fish exposed to aqueous solutions of toxic chemicals may be conducted in respirometer metabolism chambers. Anesthetized fish are immobilized by spinal transection, and inserted with a urine catheter, dorsal aortic cannula, electrodes, and attachment of an oral membrane. Predose measurements are taken before chemical exposure. Fish are monitored for 24 to 48 hours, and measurements taken every 2 hours. Ventilation rate (VR) and cough response (CR) are determined using freestanding stainless steel electrodes. Ventilation volume (V), oxygen consumption (VO), and oxygen utilization (U) may be obtained using dissolved oxygen (DO) concentrations in inspired and expired water from the chambers (McKim 1987).

method.description: Ventilation rate (VR), ventilation volume (V), oxygen consumption (VO), and oxygen utilization (U) are determined using dissolved oxygen (DO) concentrations in inspired and expired water.
method.measured-endpoint: ventilation rate, ventilation volume, oxygen consumption, oxygen utilization

evidence.source-text: Ventilation rate (VR) and cough response (CR) are determined using freestanding stainless steel electrodes.
Ventilation volume (V), oxygen consumption (VO), and oxygen utilization (U) may be obtained using dissolved oxygen (DO) concentrations in inspired and expired water from the chambers (McKim 1987).

method.description: Measures lung function in humans by assessing the ratio of volume of air expired in one second (FEV1) to forced vital capacity (FVC).

evidence.source-text: In humans, spirometry is used to measure lung function. The ratio of volume of air expired in one second (FEV1) to forced vital capacity (FVC) should be close to 80%. A decreased FEV 1/FVC is indicative of impaired ventilation.

evidence.source-text: micro-electrode array (MEA) recording has been developed and tested both in vitro (Novellino et al. 2011) and ex vivo (Dossi et al. 2014).

MEAs, which are microfabricated devices embedding an array of spatially arranged microelectrodes, provide a unique opportunity to simultaneously stimulate and record field potentials, as well as action potentials of multiple neurons from different areas of the tissue (Dossi et al. 2014).

MEAs recordings constitute an excellent tool for studying the spatio-temporal patterns of spontaneous interictal and evoked seizure-like events, the mechanisms underlying seizure onset and propagation, and electrophysiological activity of the neurons in response to chemical exposures

evidence.source-text: More definitive evidence that a substance is a CAR activator, can be attained in vivo by experiments in CAR null mice or rats, which lack the gene for the CAR molecule. method.description: Detection of actively proliferating cells by immunohistochemical staining of the endogenous protein Ki-67, which is expressed by mammalian cells in active phases of the cell cycle (G1, S, G2, M) and not expressed in quiescent (G0) cells.
method.measured-endpoint: fraction of labeled cell population/total number of cells in population

evidence.source-text: Ki-67 and PCNA are endogenous proteins expressed by mammalian cells that are in active phases of the cell cycle (G1, S, G2, M) and are not expressed in quiescent (G0) cells (Dietrich, 1993; Eldrige et al., 1993; Scholzen and Gerdes, 2000). They are detected in hepatocytes using standard immunohistochemical techniques. The advantage of using endogenous markers is that they do not require administration of exogenous markers for labeling, and they can be used for both prospective and retrospective cell proliferation analysis. A direct comparison of BrdU, Ki67 and PCNA labeling in various proliferating tissues of male Sprague-Dawley rats (Muskhelishvili et al., 2003) has indicated that Ki67 and BrdU immunohistochemistry methods gave similar labelling index results, whereas PCNA immunohistochemistry was not concordant with these methods and gave highly variable results. These authors suggested that PCNA is less accurate as a measure of cell proliferation because it has a long half-life and can be retained in cells that are not dividing, and is more involved in DNA repair mechanisms than Ki67. As a result, Ki67 has emerged as a more preferred endogenous marker for assessing cell proliferation in hepatocytes in recent years compared to PCNA.

The extent of the reaction is then measured and the area under the curve is used to determine the concentration that inhibited tubulin polymerization by 50% (IC50) [Hamel, 2003].

method.description: BrdU is a synthetic analogue of thymidine that is incorporated into DNA during the S phase of cell replication. Tissue sections are stained immunohistochemically with antibodies for BrdU and labeled cells are counted as dividing cells.

evidence.source-text: BrdU is a synthetic analogue of the nucleoside Thymidine. BrDu is incorporated into DNA synthesized during the S1 phase of cell replication and is stable for long periods. Labeling of dividing cells by BrdU is accomplished by infusion, bolus injection, or implantation of osmotic pumps containing BrdU for a period of time sufficient to generate measureable numbers of labeled cells. Tissue sections are stained immunhistochemically with antibodies for BrdU and labeled cells are counted as dividing cells.

evidence.source-text: The most common assay used is the NMDA receptor (MK801 site) radioligand competition binding assay (Reynolds and Palmer, 1991; Subramaniam and McGonigle, 1991).

Also radioligand competition binding assay can be performed using D, L-(E)-2-amino-4-[3H]-propyl-5-phosphono-3-pentenoic acid ([3H]-CGP 39653), a high affinity selective antagonist at the glutamate site of NMDA receptor, which is a quantitative autoradiography technique (Mugnaini et al., 1996).

evidence.source-text: Cancer is usually detected by biopsy or histopathological examination of tissue.

method.description: Uses CI-selective antibodies to capture Complex I from homogenates, with activity measured via NADH-dependent NBT reduction.

evidence.source-text: To assess CI activity and its inhibition in cell or tissue homogenates without interference by other components of the respiratory chain, CI-selective antibodies attached to a matrix (e.g. multiwell plates) are used (Willis et al., 2009). Homogenized tissue can directly be added for capturing of CI, the unbound supernatant is washed away and leaves a complex of the antibody and mitochondrial CI. For activity determination, NADH as electron donor and nitroblue tetrazolium (NBT) as acceptor are added. Reduced NBT forms a colored precipitate, its signal intensity is proportional to the amount of CI bound to the antibody.

process.label: mitochondrial electron transport, NADH to ubiquinone

method.measured-endpoint: NADH consumption or electron acceptor reduction

evidence.source-text: Submitochondrial particles or intact isolated mitochondria are incubated with NADH as electron donor and with an electron acceptor to measure the flow of electrons from NADH, through CI to the acceptor. As readout, either the consumption of NADH, or the reduction of the electron acceptor is followed photometrically or fluorometrically (Lenaz et al. 2004; Spinazzi et al. 2012; Long et al. 2009; Kirby et al. 2007).

process.label: mitochondrial electron transport, NADH to ubiquinone

method.description: Measures intracellular ATP levels as an indirect readout for mitochondrial function using a luminometric luciferase/luciferin assay.

evidence.source-text: ATP levels can be easily measured from lysates of in vitro cell cultures or from tissues by a luminometric luciferase/luciferin assay. The amount of light emitted is proportional to the amount of ATP in the sample (Nguyen et al. 1988, Leist et al., 1997).

method.description: Measures intracellular ATP levels in cell lysates or tissues by quantifying the light emitted during the luciferase-mediated oxidation of luciferin.

evidence.source-text: ATP levels can be easily measured from lysates of in vitro cell cultures or from tissues by a luminometric luciferase/luciferin assay. The amount of light emitted is proportional to the amount of ATP in the sample

method.description: Measures NADH/NAD+ ratios in mitochondria using imaging methods to assess mitochondrial activity.

evidence.source-text: One exemplary approach is the measurement of NADH/NAD+ ratios in mitochondria by imaging methods. This provides resolution on the level of individual mitochondria within a living cell (van Vliet et al., 2014).

process.label: mitochondrial electron transport, NADH to ubiquinone

method.description: Measures the consumption of oxygen in a closed system as a parameter for mitochondrial respiratory activity, traditionally with a Clark electrode or with optical methods. Can be performed in permeabilized cells or isolated mitochondria.

evidence.source-text: “Electrons, fed into the mitochondrial respiratory chain either by CI or complex II, ultimately reduce molecular oxygen to water at complex IV. In a closed system, this consumption of oxygen leads to a drop of the overall O2 concentration, and this can serve as parameter for mitochondrial respiratory activity.”

method.description: Measures oxygen consumption as a surrogate for mitochondrial respiratory activity using a Clark electrode.

evidence.source-text: Measurements are traditionally done with a Clark electrode, or with more sophisticated optical methods. At the cathode of a Clark electrode, oxygen is electrolytically reduced, which initiates a current in the electrode, causing a potential difference that is ultimately recorded.

process.label: mitochondrial electron transport, NADH to ubiquinone

method.description: Measures Complex I activity by observing reverse electron flow from succinate to NAD+, forming NADH.

evidence.source-text: With this method, electrons enter the respiratory chain via complex II. Based on the reverse flux, this method allows the complete circumvention of complexes III and IV. As electron donor, succinate is applied, together with NAD+ as electron acceptor. Formation of NADH from NAD+ can be determined photometrically.

process.label: mitochondrial electron transport, NADH to ubiquinone

method.description: Measures oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) in live cells using a Seahorse extracellular flux analyzer. Cells are kept in a small volume and changes in oxygen levels are detected by an oxygen sensor.

evidence.source-text: “A modern convenient method to measure oxygen consumption is provided by the Seahorse technology of extracellular flux (XF) analysis, in which cells are kept in a very small volume, so that changes of oxygen levels can be detected very sensitively by an oxygen sensor.”

method.description: Quantitative autoradiography measures binding of a radioactively labeled ligand ([3H]-dihydrorotenone) to the rotenone binding site of complex I in tissue sections. The assay detects competitive inhibitors that bind to the rotenone site by displacement of the labeled ligand.
method.measured-endpoint: binding of inhibitor to complex I rotenone site

evidence.source-text: Binding of this rotenone-derivative is detected by autoradiography. Unselective binding is determined by measurement of [3H]-DHR binding in the presence of an excess of unlabeled rotenone.

The method can be used for (a) in vitro measurements and for (b) ex vivo measurements: a) In vitro measurements. Tissues are embedded in a matrix for cutting by a cryostat. The tissue slices are then mounted onto slides. For the binding experiment, they are incubated with the test compound in the presence of labeled [3H]-DHR. Then the tissue slices are washed and prepared for autoradiographic detection (Greenamyre et al. 1992; Higgins and Greenamyre, 1996).

method.description: This assay quantifies the displacement of a radioactively labelled ligand ([3H]-dihydrorotenone) by a toxicant in tissue samples to assess binding at the rotenone binding site of Complex I. Binding is detected by autoradiography.

evidence.source-text: To assess binding of an inhibitor at the rotenone binding site of CI in tissues (e.g. in the substantia nigra or in the striatum), the standard approach is to quantify the displacement of a radioactively labelled ligand of this binding site by the toxicant under evaluation.
Most commonly, binding of [3H]-labeled dihydrorotenone (DHR) is measured and compared in control tissue and treated tissue.
Binding of this rotenone-derivative is detected by autoradiography.

method.assay-name: Autophagic flux measurement via radioactive protein turnover
method.description: Measurement of autophagic flux by assessing the rate of turnover of long-lived proteins labeled with [14C]-leucine or [14C]-valine, quantified by liquid scintillation counting.

evidence.source-text: The lysosomal degradation of the autophagic cargo constitutes the autophagic flux, which can be measured by assessing the rate of turnover of long-lived proteins that are normally turned over by autophagy (Bauvy et al., 2009). This is performed by labelling intracellular proteins with either [14C]-leucine or [14C]-valine, followed by a long culture period in standard medium. The release of radioactive leucin or valin into the culture medium corresponds to the protein degradation rate in cells, and it may be measured by liquid scintillation counting.

evidence.source-text: A range of technologies has been used to visualize mitochondrial dynamics in live cells (Jakobs, 2006; Grafstein and Forman, 1980). They usually employ a combination of mitochondrial labelling with fluorescent dyes (e.g. DiOC6 (3, 3′-Dihexyloxacarbocyanine iodide), JC-1 (5,5′,6,6′-Tetrachloro-1,1′,3,3′ tetraethylbenzimida-zolylcarbo-cyanine iodide), MitoTracker, MitoFluor probes, etc.), followed by video- or confocal microscopy for live cell imaging (Schwarz, 2013; Pool et al., 2006). Additionally, also mitochondrial fusion and fission have been monitored by such methods (Exner et al., 2012).

method.description: Acridine orange (AO) is a weak base that accumulates in acidic compartments like lysosomes. Red fluorescence indicates high concentration in acidic vesicles, while green fluorescence indicates lower concentration in other cell parts.

method.description: Total glutathione is determined using enzyme recycling, where GSH reacts with DTNB (Ellman's reagent) in the presence of glutathione reductase, producing a yellow colored product measured at 412 nm.

evidence.source-text: Enzyme recycling is a widely accepted method to determine total glutathione, in which GSH reacts with DTNB (Ellman's reagent) in the presence of glutathione reductase.

Glutathione reductase reduces GSSG to GSH, which then reacts with DTNB to produce a yellow colored 5-thio-2-nitrobenzoic acid (TNB), which absorbs light at a wavelength of 412 nm (Tipple and Rogers, 2012).

method.description: Chromatin immunoprecipitation measures the interaction of proteins with specific genomic regions in vivo. It involves crosslinking proteins and DNA, isolating nuclear fractions, shearing DNA, immunoprecipitation with an antibody, reversing crosslinking, and sequencing associated DNA fragments.

Enrichment of specific DNA sequences represents regions on the genome that the protein of interest is associated with in vivo.

method.description: Measures the interaction of proteins with specific genomic regions in vivo by crosslinking, shearing DNA, and sequencing associated DNA fragments.

evidence.source-text: Chromatin immunoprecipitation measures the interaction of proteins with specific genomic regions in vivo. It involves the treatment of cells with formaldehyde to crosslink neighboring protein-protein and protein-DNA molecules. Nuclear fractions are isolated, the genomic DNA is sheared, and nuclear lysates are used in immunoprecipitations with an antibody against the protein of interest. After reversal of the crosslinking, the associated DNA fragments are sequenced.

method.description: Electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) studies DNA-binding protein interactions in vitro by observing slower migration of protein-DNA complexes through a non-denaturing polyacrylamide gel compared to free DNA fragments. Components are identified with antibodies.

method.description: Uses ultra-high frequency ultrasound (30-70 MHz) to detect stillborn or mummified offspring or increased resorptions in mammalian pregnancies.

evidence.source-text: stillborn or mummified offspring, or an increased rate of resorptions early in pregnancy are all considered embryolethal, and can be detected using ultra-high frequency ultrasound (30-70 MHz; a.k.a. ultrasound biomicroscopy)

method.description: Vascular resistance is calculated using the formula: (mean arterial pressure minus mean right arterial pressure) divided by cardiac output.

evidence.source-text: Vascular resistance cannot be measured by any direct means, but can be calculated using a formula: (mean arterial pressure minus mean right arterial pressure) divided by cardiac output (Siddiqui 2011).

method.description: Measures average blood pressure over a 24-hour period, providing daytime and nighttime averages.

evidence.source-text: Stage 1 hypertension : Clinic blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg or higher and subsequent ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) daytime average or home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) average blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg or higher.
Stage 2 hypertension : Clinic blood pressure is 160/100 mmHg or higher and subsequent ABPM daytime average or HBPM average blood pressure is 150/95 mmHg or higher.

method.description: Measures binding affinity between TTR and ligands using a fluorescent probe that is displaced by the ligand, resulting in a decrease in fluorescence intensity.

evidence.source-text: Cao et al (2010) used a novel fluorescence displacement method using a protein-binding probe that fluoresces when bound, and the intensity of which dips following displacement for a ligand.

Ren and Guo (2012) reported use of a non-radioactive, fluorescin-T4 conjugate designed as a fluorescent probe (vs ANSA probe which is less TTR-specific) to study the binding interaction of multiple hydroxylated PBDEs with differing degrees of bromination and differing hydroxy positions and TTR.
Ren et al (2016) used a fluorescence displacement assay to study 16 PFCs and found T4 to have an IC50 of 31 nM (Kd = 5 nM), as compared to PFOS (the strongest binder) TC50 of 130 nM (Kd = 20 nM).

method.description: Biochemical approaches using GC/MS or LC/MS are used to measure binding affinity using recombinant TTR, with limits of detection in the low nM range.

evidence.source-text: Biochemical (in chemico) approaches using GC/MS or LC/MS also exist that use recombinant (rTTR) and display limits of detection in the low nM range, including a multi-mode, ultra-high-performance LC method and anon-radioactive label, [13C6]-T4 (Aqai et al 2012).

method.description: Measures binding affinity between TTR and ligands using mass spectrometry to quantify ligand concentrations in biochemical assays.
method.measured-endpoint: ligand concentration (limits of detection in low nM range)

evidence.source-text: Biochemical (in chemico) approaches using GC/MS or LC/MS also exist that use recombinant (rTTR) and display limits of detection in the low nM range, including a multi-mode, ultra-high-performance LC method and a non-radioactive label, [13C6]-T4 (Aqai et al 2012).
