method.description: Measures binding affinity between TTR and ligands using radiolabeled T4 and gel-filtration to separate bound and free ligand.

evidence.source-text: Van den Berg et al (1991) used an in vitro competitive radioligand binding assay with gel-filtration procedure modified from Somack et al (1982) as well to screen 65 compounds from 12 chemical classes for evidence of interference with the T4 binding site of TTR using a radioligand binding assay and reported results semi-quantitatively

Lans et al (1993, 1994) used purified TTR and T4 [125I] as a displaceable radioligand and gel-filtration procedure modified from Somack et al (1982) to study hydroxylated PCBs PCDDs and PCDFs and found many competitive binders in all classes
Weiss et al (2009) initially determined the competitive binding of TTR with PFCs via radioligand-binding assay of Hamers et al (2006) and Lans et al (1993)

method.description: Measures binding affinity between TTR and ligands using a surface-based biosensor to detect interactions in real-time.

evidence.source-text: Marchesini et al (2006, 2008) reported a surface plasmon resonance biosensor-based method using rTTR, a surface-based measurement which may not fully characterize the binding reaction of a homogenous solution or matrix. Optimized SPR is more sensitive, amenable to high-throughput screening and easier to perform than RLBAs.

method.description: Directly measures free T4 and T3 concentrations by separating bound from unbound hormone.

evidence.source-text: Total T4 is most often measured using human serum based diagnostic kits, but free T4 (and T3) is only directly measured through equilibrium dialysis and ultrafiltration (Midgley 2001).

method.description: Measures displacement of T4 from TTR using a protein-binding fluorescent probe (ANSA) that becomes highly fluorescent after binding to T4.

evidence.source-text: Cao et al 2010, Cao et al 2011 and Ren and Guo 2012 developed the FLU-TTR, based on a protein-binding fluorescent probe (ANSA, or 8-anilo-1-naphthalenesulfonic acid ammonium salt) that becomes highly fluorescent after binding to T4.
This allows generation of binding constant (K) data as opposed to past efforts that generated IC50 values.

method.description: An assay using fluorescent probes (e.g., ANSA) that bind to T4; displacement of the probe by a compound of interest reduces fluorescence.

evidence.source-text: developed the FLU-TTR, based on a protein-binding fluorescent probe... that becomes highly fluorescent after binding to T4. When the compound of interest is introduced and displaces the ANSA-thyroxine probe, this fluorescence is reduced.
This allows generation of binding constant (K) data

method.description: Fluorescence-based assay using a protein-binding fluorescent probe (ANSA) that becomes highly fluorescent upon binding to T4; displacement by a compound of interest reduces fluorescence, allowing calculation of binding constants (K).
method.measured-endpoint: displacement of T4 from TTR/TBG via fluorescence reduction

evidence.source-text: Cao et al 2010, Cao et al 2011 and Ren and Guo 2012 developed the FLU-TTR, based on a protein-binding fluorescent probe (ANSA, or 8-anilo-1-naphthalenesulfonic acid ammonium salt) that becomes highly fluorescent after binding to T4. When the compound of interest is introduced and displaces the ANSA-thyroxine probe, this fluorescence is reduced.
This allows generation of binding constant (K) data as opposed to past efforts that generated IC50 values.
Cao et al 2011 developed a fluorescent microtiter method for pTTR and TBG tested with bisphenol A.

method.description: Uses polyclonal TTR antibodies covalently bound to sepharose resin to isolate TTR from plasma, followed by HPLC analysis.

evidence.source-text: Purkey et al 2001 published a binding assay using polyclonal TTR antibodies covalently bound to sepharose resin which is then mixed with plasma pre-treated with compound of interest, washed and analyzed via HPLC.

method.description: The immunoprecipitation-HPLC assay uses polyclonal TTR antibodies covalently bound to sepharose resin. Plasma pre-treated with compound of interest is mixed with the resin, washed, and analyzed via HPLC to measure the displacement of T4 from TTR.

evidence.source-text: Purkey et al 2001 published a binding assay using polyclonal TTR antibodies covalently bound to sepharose resin which is then mixed with plasma pre-treated with compound of interest, washed and analyzed via HPLC.

method.assay-name: isotope-free competitive binding assay with UPLC-MS
method.description: Isotope-free competitive binding assay using 13C6-T4 to screen thyroid transport protein ligands for recombinant TTR, employing immunomagnetic beads followed by flow cytometry and UPLC-MS detection.
method.measured-endpoint: binding of T4 analogs to TTR

evidence.source-text: Aqai et al 2012 described a rapid and isotope-free (13C6-T4) screening of thyroid transport protein ligands, using a competitive binding assay for rTTR using fast ultrahigh performance LC-electrospray ionization triple-quadrupole MS.
The method involves the use of immunomagnetic beads followed by screening with flow cytometry and UPLC-MS.
The high-throughput screening mode is capable of detecting T4 in water at the part-per-trillion level and in the part-per-billion level in urine.

evidence.source-text: The EPA ToxCast Phase I efforts used quantitative nuclease protection assays (qNPA) to screen several hundred chemicals for UGT1A1 and SULT2A1 (Rotroff et al 2010, Sinz et al 2006).

method.description: Radioligand binding assays use [125I]-T4 as a label to demonstrate affinity for xenobiotics to human or rat transthyretin (TTR). The most commonly used method was first published by Somack et al 1982 and adapted by Hamers et al 2006, Lans et al 1993 and Ucan-Marin et al 2010. The assay involves purified TTR from human serum and is performed in a pure aqueous solution.

evidence.source-text: Radioligand binding assays, using [125I]-T4 as a label, were developed to demonstrate affinity for xenobiotics to human or rat TTR and TBG (Brouwer and van den Berg 1986, Lans et al 1994).
The most commonly used method was first published by Somack et al 1982 and adapted by Hamers et al 2006, Lans et al 1993 and Ucan-Marin et al 2010.
Similar assays have been developed using [125I]-T3 as a label for affinity to chicken and bullfrog TTR (Yamauchi et al 2003).

method.description: Measures displacement of T4 from serum transport proteins using [125I]-T4 as a label to demonstrate affinity for xenobiotics to human or rat TTR and TBG.

evidence.source-text: Radioligand binding assays, using [125I]-T4 as a label, were developed to demonstrate affinity for xenobiotics to human or rat TTR and TBG (Brouwer and van den Berg 1986, Lans et al 1994).

method.description: In vitro assay using [125I]-T4 or [125I]-T3 as a radioligand to measure affinity of xenobiotics for human/rat TTR or TBG via a wash/separation procedure to quantify displaced free T4.

evidence.source-text: Radioligand binding assays, using [125I]-T4 as a label, were developed to demonstrate affinity for xenobiotics to human or rat TTR and TBG (Brouwer and van den Berg 1986, Lans et al 1994).
The most commonly used method was first published by Somack et al 1982 and adapted by Hamers et al 2006, Lans et al 1993 and Ucan-Marin et al 2010.
Radioligand methods suffer from having to use heavily regulated isotopes and lower throughput to provide free T4 measurements (due to the extra wash/separation procedure needed).

method.description: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) biosensor assays use recombinant TTR and TBG to measure the binding of compounds to these transport proteins. The assay was developed by Marchesini et al 2006 and validated with known thyroid disruptors and structurally related compounds.
method.measured-endpoint: binding affinity of compounds to TTR and TBG

evidence.source-text: Marchesini et al 2006 reported on the development of two surface plasmon resonance(SPR)-based biosensor assays using recombinant TTR and TBG, validated with known thyroid disruptors and structurally related compounds including halogenated phenols, polychlorinated biphenyls, bisphenols and a hydroxylated PCB metabolite (4-OH-CB 14).
TH is covalently bound to a gold-layered chip and a mixture of the compound of interest and transport protein are injected in a flow cell passing over the bound TH.

method.description: A biosensor-based assay using recombinant TTR or TBG and a gold-layered chip to measure the displacement of thyroid hormones by compounds of interest.

evidence.source-text: two surface plasmon resonance(SPR)-based biosensor assays using recombinant TTR and TBG

method.description: Measures the phosphatase activity of calcineurin (CN) using a phosphatase assay. method.description: Measures deiodinase activities by quantifying the radioactive iodine release from iodine-labelled substrates.

evidence.source-text: A first in vitro assay measures deiodinase activities by quantifying the radioactive iodine release from iodine-labelled substrates, depending on the preferred substrates of the isoforms of deiodinases (Forhead et al., 2006; Pavelka, 2010; Houbrechts et al., 2016; Stinckens et al., 2018). Each of these assays requires a source of deiodinase which can be obtained for example using unexposed pig liver tissue (available from slaughterhouses) or rat liver tissue.

method.description: A nonradioactive assay measuring iodide released using a photometric method based on Ce4+ reduction.

evidence.source-text: Olker et al. (2019) on the other hand used an adenovirus expression system to produce the DIO2 enzyme and developed an assay for nonradioactive measurement of iodide released using the Sandell-Kolthoff method, a photometric method based on Ce4+ reduction (Renko et al., 2012). This assay was then used to screen the ToxCast Phase 1 chemical library.

method.assay-name: ToxCast Estrogen Receptor Agonist Pathway Model
method.description: Predicts ER agonism or antagonism using activity patterns from 18 high-throughput screening assays.

evidence.source-text: ToxCast Estrogen Receptor Agonist Pathway Model: The ToxCast estrogen receptor (ER) pathway model is a mathematical model that combines the results from 18 high-throughput screening (HTS) assays from the ToxCast and Tox21 research programs. The HTS assays measure ER binding, dimerization, chromatin binding, transcriptional activation and ER-dependent cell proliferation. The model uses activity patterns across the in vitro assays to predict whether a chemical is an ER agonist or antagonist or is otherwise influencing the assays through a manner dependent on the physics and chemistry of the technology platform (“assay interference”). The output of the model provides an area under the curve (AUC) value for the potential of a chemical to cause ER agonism, normalized with respect to the positive control chemical, oestradiol.

method.description: Measures the contraction force of the anterior byssus retractor muscle (ABRM) in bivalves after stimulation with acetylcholine. The assay quantifies the ability of the muscle to maintain a contracted state with minimal energy expenditure after the initial stimulus has ceased.

evidence.source-text: In bivalves, the muscle involved in valve movement is the anterior byssus retractor muscle (ABRM). This muscle and other muscles can undergo a catch state of contraction, which is characterized by a very slowly decaying force in the absence of stimulation.

When contraction of the ABRM (and other catch-capable muscles) is initiated by the neurotransmitter acetylcholine, it contracts actively and remains in the contracted state with minimal energetic investment (Güth et al. 1984; Butler et al. 1998) even after the acetylcholine stimulation has ceased and internal calcium stores are returned to basal levels(Ishii et al. 1989).
This unique physiology allows the muscle to maintain a closed valve without depleting energy reserves.

method.description: This assay measures the force generated by the anterior byssus retractor muscle (ABRM) over time, specifically focusing on the slowly decaying force characteristic of the catch state contraction. The assay assesses the muscle's ability to maintain contraction with minimal energy expenditure.

A reproducible high-throughput application of the assay is available (Ge, Prasongtanakij et al. 2014; Sykora, Witt et al. 2018), and the test requires only a small (single cell) sample.

evidence.source-text: Cytokine mRNAs were detected using a RiboQuant MultiProbe RPA system (PharMingen, San Diego, CA). Riboprobes were 32P-labeled and hybridized overnight with 10 to 30 mg of the RNA samples. The hybridized RNA was treated with RNase and purified according to the RiboQuant protocol. The samples were then electrophoresed in 6% polyacrylamide-Tris-borate-EDTA-urea gels using the Seqi -Gen GT Nucleic Acid Electrophoresis Cell (Bio-Rad, Hercules, CA), or minigels (Novex, San Diego, CA). The gels were dried, exposed and quantitated in a PhosphorImager (Molecular Dynamics, Sunnyvale, CA) using the ImageQuant software (Dumont et al. 1998).

method.description: Diffusion capacity of carbon monoxide (DLCO) studies measure gas exchange across the alveolar-capillary barrier by assessing the increased affinity of hemoglobin for carbon monoxide. It provides information about the lung surface area available for gas diffusion.

evidence.source-text: Finally, indices of gas exchange across the alveolar-capillary barrier are tested by diffusion capacity of carbon monoxide (DLCO) studies (also referred to as transfer capacity of carbon monoxide, TLCO).
The principle of the test is the increased affinity of hemoglobin to preferentially bind carbon monoxide over oxygen (Weinstock and McCannon, 2017).
Complementary to spirometry and lung volume measurements, DLCO provides information about the lung surface area available for gas diffusion.

method.description: Helium dilution measures lung volumes by inhaling a known volume and concentration of helium and measuring the final concentration. FRC is then calculated based on the dilution.

evidence.source-text: In the helium dilution method, a known volume and concentration of helium is inhaled by the subject.
Helium, an inert gas that is not absorbed significantly from the lungs, is diluted in proportion to the lung volume to which it is added.
The final concentration of helium is then measured and FRC calculated (Weinstock and McCannon, 2017).

method.description: Nitrogen washout measures lung volumes by administering 100% oxygen and collecting expired gas until no nitrogen is detected. The initial volume of the system (FRC) is then calculated.

evidence.source-text: The nitrogen washout method is based on the fact that nitrogen is present in the air, at a relatively constant amount.
The subject is given 100% oxygen to breathe, and the expired gas, which contains nitrogen in the lung at the beginning of the test, is collected.
When no more nitrogen is noted in the expirate, the volume of air expired and the entire amount of nitrogen in that volume are measured, and the initial volume of the system (FRC) can be calculated.

method.description: Plethysmography measures functional residual capacity (FRC), expiratory reserve volume (ERV), vital capacity (VC), inspiratory capacity (IC), total lung capacity (TLC), and residual volume (RV) in a body plethysmograph. It can be used in both conscious and anesthetized animals.

evidence.source-text: Plethysmography consists of a series of sequential measurements in a body plethysmograph, starting with the measurement of functional residual capacity (FRC)

In small laboratory animals, plethysmography can be used to determine respiratory physiology parameters (minute volume, respiratory rate, time of pause and time of break), lung volume and airway resistance of conscious animals.

Both whole body and head-out plethysmography can be applied, although there is a preference for the latter in the context of inhalation toxicity studies, because of its higher accuracy and reliability (OECD, 2018a; Hoymann, 2012).

method.description: Spirometry measures several different parameters during forceful exhalation, including FEV1, FVC, VC, FEV1/FVC ratio, PEF, and forced expiratory flow. It is used for diagnostic purposes and determining the degree of lung function impairment.
method.guideline: ATS/ERS Task Force guidelines (Graham et al., 2019)

evidence.source-text: The most common (“gold standard”) lung function test in human subjects is spirometry.
Spirometry results are primarily used for diagnostic purposes, e.g. to discriminate between obstructive and restrictive lung diseases, and for determining the degree of lung function impairment.
Specific criteria for spirometry tests have been outlined in the American Thoracic Society (ATS) and the European Respiratory Society (ERS) Task Force guidelines (Graham et al., 2019).

method.description: Assesses fibrotic lung disease by morphometric analysis of diseased area versus total lung area using a numerical scale (Ashcroft score).

evidence.source-text: histopathological analysis is used for assessing fibrotic lung disease. Morphometric analysis of the diseased area versus total lung area is used to quantitatively stage the fibrotic disease.
a numerical scale with grades from 0 to 8, originally developed by Ashcroft et al., 1988 is assigned to indicate the amount of fibrotic tissue in histological samples.

method.description: Histopathological analysis of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded lung tissue sections is used to assess fibrotic lung disease. The amount of fibrotic tissue is staged using a numerical scale from 0 to 8 originally developed by Ashcroft et al., 1988, with modifications proposed by Hubner et al., 2008, applied to grade fibrosis in both human and animal samples.
method.measured-endpoint: fibrotic tissue area in lung histological samples

evidence.source-text: In vivo, histopathological analysis is used for assessing fibrotic lung disease.
Morphometric analysis of the diseased area versus total lung area is used to quantitatively stage the fibrotic disease.
a numerical scale with grades from 0 to 8, originally developed by Ashcroft et al., 1988 is assigned to indicate the amount of fibrotic tissue in histological samples.
This scale is applied to diagnose lung fibrosis in both human and animal samples.
Modifications to this scoring system were proposed (Hubner et al., 2008), which enables morphological distinctions thus enabling a better grading of the disease.

bleomycin induced lung fibrosis in rats was scored as follows: Grade 0 – normal lung, Grade 1 – isolated alveolar septa with gentle fibrotic changes, Grade 2 – knot like formation in fibrotic areas in alveolar septa, Grade 3 – contiguous fibrotic walls of alveolar septa, Grade 4 – single fibrotic masses, Grade 5 – confluent fibrotic masses, Grade 6 – large contiguous fibrotic masses, Grade 7 – air bubbles and Grade 8 – fibrotic obliteration.

method.description: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded lung cross-sections are imaged using a wide field light microscope. ImageJ software is used to trace and quantify the total and diseased areas, calculating the diseased area as a proportion of the total area.

evidence.source-text: Lungs are formalin fixed and paraffin embedded such that an entire cross section of lung can be presented on a slide.
ImageJ software (freely available) is used to trace the total area (green line) and the diseased area (red line) imaged and quantified.
The diseased area is equal to disease area/total area (Nikota et al., 2017).

method.description: Measures net CO₂ uptake non-invasively, allowing continuous monitoring of photosynthetic performance under controlled environmental conditions.

evidence.source-text: At the whole-organism or leaf level, infrared gas analysis (IRGA) is commonly employed to measure net CO₂ uptake. This non-invasive technique allows continuous monitoring of photosynthetic performance under controlled environmental conditions and integrates stomatal conductance, biochemical capacity, and photochemical efficiency into a single functional endpoint.

method.description: Quantifies the rate of O₂ production under illumination using Clark-type oxygen electrodes or polarographic methods, providing a measure of Photosystem II activity.

evidence.source-text: Oxygen evolution measurements offer a direct proxy for the activity of the photosynthetic light reactions, particularly Photosystem II. Using Clark-type oxygen electrodes or polarographic methods, the rate of O₂ production under illumination can be quantified in intact tissues, leaf discs, or isolated chloroplasts, providing sensitive detection of functional impairment in the photosynthetic electron transport chain.

method.description: Quantifies the catalytic capacity of ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase using ¹⁴C-based assays or NADH-linked spectrophotometric methods.

evidence.source-text: To resolve downstream biochemical constraints, Rubisco activity assays are used to quantify the catalytic capacity of ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase. Both ¹⁴C-based assays and NADH-linked spectrophotometric or microtiter plate methods enable discrimination between limitations arising from carbon fixation enzymes versus upstream photochemical processes.

method.description: Quantifies the incorporation of inorganic carbon into organic compounds during photosynthesis, providing an integrative measure of photosynthetic carbon assimilation.

evidence.source-text: Carbon fixation rates are most directly assessed using ¹⁴C-bicarbonate uptake assays, which quantify the incorporation of inorganic carbon into organic compounds during photosynthesis.

method.description: Measures calcein release into media following hydrolysis of calcein AM by intracellular esterases in cells with compromised membranes.

evidence.source-text: The Calcein AM assay depends on the hydrolysis of calcein AM (a non-fluorescent hydrophobic compound that permeates live cells by simple diffusion) by non-specific intracellular esterases resulting in production of calcein, a hydrophilic and strongly fluorescent compound that is readily released into the cell culture media by the damaged cells.

method.description: Measures lactate dehydrogenase released into the media following cell membrane injury, quantified via NAD reduction and tetrazolium dye conversion.

evidence.source-text: Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release assay is a very sensitive cytotoxicity assay that measures the amount of LDH released in the media following membrane injury. The assay is based on measuring the reduction of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and conversion of a tetrazolium dye that is measured at a wavelength of 490 nm.

method.description: Measures transepithelial/transendothelial electrical resistance to assess tight junction integrity in cell monolayers.

evidence.source-text: Transepithelial/transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER) is an accepted quantitative technique that measures the integrity of tight junctions in cell culture models of endothelial and epithelial cell monolayers.

Advanced in vitro co-culture models, like the EpiAlveolar model system, and other similar systems present an intact capillary membrane that can be used to assess loss in the membrane integrity (via TEER) after exposure to pro-fibrotic stressors like crystalline silica and Transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) (Barasova et al., 2020, Kasper et al., 2011).

method.description: A dye exclusion assay where intact cells exclude trypan blue, while cells with compromised membranes take up the dye and appear blue.

evidence.source-text: The most commonly employed method is the trypan blue exclusion assay – a dye exclusion assay where cells with intact membrane do not permit entry of the dye into cells and thus remain clear, whereas the dye diffuses into cells with damaged membrane turning them to blue colour.

method.description: A dye exclusion assay where cells with intact membranes remain clear, while cells with damaged membranes take up the dye and turn blue, indicating cytotoxicity.

evidence.source-text: Cellular viability or cytotoxicity assays are the most commonly used endpoints to assess the leaky or compromised cell membrane. The most commonly employed method is the trypan blue exclusion assay – a dye exclusion assay where cells with intact membrane do not permit entry of the dye into cells and thus remain clear, whereas the dye diffuses into cells with damaged membrane turning them to blue colour.

evidence.source-text: Apart from assaying single protein or gene at a time, cytokine bead arrays or cytokine PCR arrays can be used to detect a whole panel of Th1 and/or Th2 cytokines using a multiplex method. method.description: ELISA is used to assess the levels of protein of several Th1 and Th2 cytokines including IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, IL-10, IL-12, IFN-γ, and TGF-β. BALF supernatant, tissue homogenates, or cell pellets can be used.

evidence.source-text: Targeted enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA) or real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) (routinely used and recommended):
The ELISA and qRT-PCR are routinely used to assess the levels of protein and mRNA of several Th1 and Th2 cytokines including IL-4, IL-5, IL- 13, IL-10, IL-12, IFN-γ .
BALF supernatant collected from lungs of animals exposed to toxic substances or human patients is used. Tissue homogenates or cell pellets can also be used.

method.description: Assessment of myofibroblast differentiation using co-culture models that mimic the alveolar capillary membrane. Immunofluorescent staining for α-SMA is used to detect differentiation.

evidence.source-text: Advanced co-culture models (myofibroblast differentiation): Co-culture models that mimic the alveolar capillary membrane (such as those listed for Event 1496 & Event 1498) can be used to assess myofibroblast differentiation in response to pro-fibrotic stressors using immunofluorescent staining for α-SMA.

method.description: Uses hydrogels (e.g., collagen, fibrin) to mimic ECM and assess fibroblast proliferation, activation, and matrix synthesis.
method.measured-endpoint: cell proliferation, activation, and matrix synthesis

evidence.source-text: Hydrogels can be prepared to express inherent biological signals, mechanical properties (e.g., modulus) and biochemical properties (e.g., proteins) of the ECM. Fibroblasts are usually cultured in fibrin and type-1 collagen that represent the matrix of the wound healing. Thus, the well-constructed hydrogel can be used to assess cell proliferation, activation and matrix synthesis as reflective of fibroblast activation.

method.description: Myofibroblast differentiation is assessed using immunofluorescent staining for α-SMA in co-culture models mimicking the alveolar capillary membrane or microfluidic lung-on-a-chip models.

evidence.source-text: Co-culture models that mimic the alveolar capillary membrane (such as those listed for Event 1496 & Event 1498) can be used to assess myofibroblast differentiation in response to pro-fibrotic stressors using immunofluorescent staining for α-SMA.
More complex in vitro microfluidic lung-on-a-chip models (such as the one listed for Event 1497) can be used to assess myofibroblast differentiation in the same stead.

method.measured-endpoint: number of cells expressing fibroblast/myofibroblast markers

evidence.source-text: Proliferation of fibroblasts and activation of myofibroblasts is normally detected using individual antibodies against vimentin, procollagen 1 and α-SMA, specific markers of fibroblasts and myofibroblasts (Zhang, 1994).

Although only semiquantitative, morphometric analysis of the lung slices can be conducted to quantify the total number of cells expressing the markers against the control lung sections where expression of specific markers is expected to be low or nil.

method.description: Measurement of fibroblast proliferation using water-soluble tetrazolium salts (WST)-1 and propidium iodide staining. Dose-dependent increase in MWCNT-induced fibroblast proliferation.

evidence.source-text: Fibroblast proliferation assay: Several primary and immortalised fibroblast types can be used for the assay. Proliferation assays such as water-soluble tetrazolium salts (WST)-1 and propidium iodide staining of cells have been used to show dose-dependent increase in MWCNT-induced increase in fibroblast proliferation that is in alignment with in vivo mouse fibrogenic response (Azad et al., 2013; Vietti et al., 2013) to the same material.

evidence.source-text: In vitro, expression of type-1 collagen, Thy-1 cell surface antigen (Thy-1), cyclooxygenase-2 (COX2) and caveolin-1 (CAV1) are used as markers of homogeneous population of fibroblasts.
Increased expression of Transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) and α-SMA is used as markers of differentiated myofibroblasts.
Transcription factor SMAD family member 3 (Smad3) is the other marker measured in vitro to assess the fibroblast proliferation and differentiation.

method.description: The Hydroxyproline Assay measures the amount of hydroxyproline, a non-proteinogenic amino acid found only in collagen, to quantify collagen levels.

evidence.source-text: Hydroxyproline is a non-proteinogenic amino acid formed by the prolyl-4-hydroxylase. Hydroxyproline is only found in collagen and thus, it serves as a direct measure of the amount of collagen present in cells or tissues. Colorimetric methods are readily available and have been extensively used to quantify collagen using this assay (Chen & Raghunath, 2009; Nikota et al., 2017).

method.description: Detects apoptosis by measuring the binding of annexin V to phosphatidylserine exposed on the outer membrane of apoptotic cells.

evidence.source-text: An older but effective technique it the annexin V – affinity assay. The principle of this assay is the high affinity binding between annexin V and phosphatidylserine. In a vital cell there is a membrane lipid asymmetry where phosphatidylserine molecules are facing the cytosol. During apoptosis the membrane lipid asymmetry is lost, and the phosphatidylserine molecules are expressed in the outer membrane. When annexin-V is present in combination with Ca2+ it binds with high affinity to phosphatidylserine.

method.description: Detects phosphatidylserine exposure on the outer cell membrane, a hallmark of early apoptosis, using annexin V binding.

method.description: Provides high-resolution optical imaging with depth selectivity to visualize cellular uptake of nanoparticles.

evidence.source-text: Evaluation of NP cellular uptake by confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). CLSM combines high-resolution optical imaging with depth selectivity which allows optical sectioning. The CLSM works by passing a laser beam through a light source aperture which is focused by an objective lens into a small area on the surface of the sample and an image is built up pixel-by-pixel by collecting the emitted photons from the fluorophores in the sample (Harush-Frenkel et al., 2006; Zhang and Monteiro-Riviere, 2009).

method.description: Spectrophotometric measurement of mitochondrial complex III activity by monitoring the reduction of cytochrome c at 550 nm using decylubiquinol as an artificial electron donor. The antimycin-sensitive rate is calculated by subtracting the antimycin-insensitive rate from the total rate.

evidence.source-text: The decylubiquinol/cytochrome c reductase assay is the standard spectrophotometric method to measure the enzymatic activity of mitochondrial complex III (ubiquinol–cytochrome c reductase) (Krähenbühl et. al, 1994).

Decylubiquinol is oxidized by complex III at the Qo site of cytochrome b, and the released electrons are transferred sequentially through the Rieske iron–sulfur protein and cytochrome c₁ subunit to the terminal electron acceptor, cytochrome c.
The rate of cytochrome c reduction is directly proportional to the activity of complex III in the sample (Krähenbühl et. al, 1994).

method.description: Measures the enzymatic activity of mitochondrial complex III by monitoring the reduction of cytochrome c at 550 nm using decylubiquinol as an electron donor.

evidence.source-text: The decylubiquinol/cytochrome c reductase assay is the standard spectrophotometric method to measure the enzymatic activity of mitochondrial complex III (ubiquinol–cytochrome c reductase) (Krähenbühl et. al, 1994).

method.description: Slide chambers coated with kinesins are used to evaluate microtubule gliding velocity, trajectory curvature, and length by visualizing rhodamine-labeled microtubules.

evidence.source-text: Kinesin-driven microtubule gliding assay: Slide chambers are covered with kinesins which adhere e.g. to specific antibodies on the glass slides. Rhodamine-labelled tubulin and unlabelled tubulin are mixed and assembled to microtubule structures. Microtubules are applied to the chamber and the rhodamine fluorescence is visualized to evaluate microtubule gliding. Microtubule-bodies are located and tracked to collect data on gliding velocity, trajectory curvature and microtubule length.

method.description: This assay measures CYP17A1 enzyme activity using isolated microsomes containing the enzyme system and P450-oxidoreductase. NADPH is added as an electron source, and substrate removal or product formation is measured to assess activity.

evidence.source-text: Inhibition of CYP17A1 can be assessed in vitro by modulating mammalian or yeast cells to express the enzyme as well as P450-oxidoreductase with/without B5. Subsequently, enzyme activity can be studied in isolated microsomes that contain the enzyme system.
The reaction substrate is added and either the substrate removal or product formation is measured (Yoshimoto & Auchus, 2015).

In the case of examining the ability of a chemical to inhibit the enzyme activity, the chemical is added in increasing concentrations and a constant level of substrate is added – a decreased conversion of the substrate to product, would suggest enzyme inhibition.

method.description: Assesses inhibition of CYP17A1 activity by measuring substrate removal or product formation in isolated microsomes or purified enzyme systems with NADPH.

evidence.source-text: Inhibition of CYP17A1 can be assessed in vitro by modulating mammalian or yeast cells to express the enzyme as well as P450-oxidoreductase with/without B5. Subsequently, enzyme activity can be studied in isolated microsomes that contain the enzyme system. Alternatively, the isolated enzyme can be used for activity measurement in concert with purified P450-oxidoreductase with/without B5. NADPH should be added as the source of electrons for the reaction to take place. The reaction substrate is added and either the substrate removal or product formation is measured (Yoshimoto & Auchus, 2015).

In the case of examining the ability of a chemical to inhibit the enzyme activity, the chemical is added in increasing concentrations and a constant level of substrate is added – a decreased conversion of the substrate to product, would suggest enzyme inhibition.

method.description: Measures the ability of chemicals to inhibit the activity of 5α-reductase enzymes using transfected cell lines or isolated enzymes.

evidence.source-text: Assessing the ability of chemicals to inhibit the activity of 5α-reductase is challenging, but has been assessed using transfected cell lines. This has been demonstrated in HEK-293 cells stably transfected with human 5α-reductase type 1, 2, and 3 (Yamana et al., 2010), in CHO cells stably transfected with human 5α-reductase type 1 and 2 (Thigpens et al., 1993), and COS cells transfected with human and rat 5α-reductase with unspecified isoforms (Andersson & Russell, 1990).
The output of the above methods could be decreased dihydrotestosterone (DHT) with increasing test chemical concentrations.

The use of radiolabeled steroids has historic and continued use for 5α-reductase inhibition examination (Andersson & Russell, 1990; Peng et al., 2020; Thigpens et al., 1993; Yamana et al., 2010); however, alternative methods are available, such as conventional ELISA kits or advanced analytical methods such as liquid chromatography coupled to tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).

method.description: Activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) measures the time taken for fibrin clot formation after the addition of calcium to phospholipid and contact activator-treated plasma, reflecting the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways.
method.measured-endpoint: time taken for fibrin clot formation

evidence.source-text: Activated partial prothrombin time (APTT). Platelet poor plasma [PPP] is incubated at 37°C then phospholipid (cephalin) and a contact activator (e.g. Kaolin, micronized silica, or ellagic acid) are added. This leads to the conversion of Factor XI [FXI] to FXIa. The remainder of the pathway is not activated as no calcium is present. The addition of calcium (pre-warmed to 37°C) initiates clotting. The APTT is the time taken from the addition of calcium to the formation of a fibrin clot.

method.description: Measures fibrinogen concentration by clotting diluted plasma with a high concentration of thrombin and comparing the clotting time to a calibration curve.

evidence.source-text: Decreased fibrinogen concentrations. Diluted plasma is clotted with a high concentration of Thrombin. The tested plasma is diluted (usually 1:10 but this may vary if the Fibrinogen concentration is very low or very high) to minimize the effect of 'inhibitory substances' within the plasma e.g. heparin, elevated levels of FDPs. The use of a high concentration of Thrombin (typically 100 U/ml) ensures that the clotting times are independent of Thrombin concentration over a wide range of Fibrinogen levels.

method.description: Measures circulating neutrophil-platelet complexes in whole blood using fluorescence-labelling of platelets and leukocytes, quantified as the percentage of leukocytes staining for a platelet-specific marker.
method.measured-endpoint: percentage of leukocytes with platelet markers

evidence.source-text: Flow cytometry is the method of choice to measure circulating neutrophil-platelet complexes in both humans and animals. This technique is based on fluorescence-labelling of platelets and leukocytes in whole blood. Characteristic side scatter properties of leukocyte subtypes already permit basic discrimination of platelets binding to neutrophils, monocytes and lymphocytes. However, leukocyte subtype-specific antibodies generate more accurate data. The endpoint is quantified as the percentage of total leukocytes (i.e. neutrophils) that also stain for a platelet-specific marker.

method.description: DNA synthesis inhibitors (hydroxyurea and 1-β-d-arabinofuranosyl cytosine) are used to convert bulky lesions into detectable single-strand breaks (SSBs) in HepaRG™ cells. The percentage of DNA in the comet tail is proportional to the level of strand breaks.

evidence.source-text: This variation of the assay uses DNA synthesis inhibitors to convert bulky lesions into detectable SSBs. HepaCometChip uses Hydroxyurea (HU) and 1-β-d-arabinofuranosyl cytosine (AraC) to detect SSBs formed from bulky adducts in the presence of the high metabolism of HepaRG™ cells. HU inhibits the enzyme ribonucleotide reductase. This enzyme mediates the synthesis of deoxyribonucleotides (dNTPs). When it is inhibited dNTPs are depleted which inhibits NER. AraC’s structure allows it to be incorporated into DNA and interrupts DNA elongation. HU and AraC delay the removal of NER and SSB intermediates. The prolonged presence of NER intermediates are indicators of bulky lesions and can be observed as comet detectable SSBs. The number of bulky lesions is then measured by detecting the % of DNA found in the tail of the comet compared to untreated samples. Percentage DNA in the comet tail is proportional to the level of strand breaks.

evidence.source-text: MCC has been assessed traditionally following inhalation of radio-labeled particles such as 99Tcm-labeled polystyrene particles, resin particles or serum albumin and following their clearance at regular intervals by radioimaging using gamma cameras (Agnew et al., 1986; Kärjä et al., 1982).

method.description: Measures nasal mucociliary clearance by timing the transport of saccharin from the nasal cavity to the nasopharynx, where its taste is perceived.

evidence.source-text: Probably one of the simplest methods is the saccharin transit test (STT). For this test, a small particle of saccharin is placed behind the anterior end of the inferior turbinate. The saccharin will be transported by mucociliary action toward the nasopharynx, where its sweet taste is perceived. When MCC is impaired, saccharin transit times will increase, with a 10- to 20-minute delay being considered a clinical sign of decreased MCC.

evidence.source-text: IHC detects Bax protein expression in tissue sections. After tissue fixation and antigen retrieval, Bax-specific antibodies are applied, followed by an enzyme-conjugated secondary antibody. A chromogenic substrate (e.g., DAB) generates a color reaction, allowing visualization under a microscope, which is useful for studying tissue-specific expression (4,8).

method.description: Detects Bax mRNA expression by isolating RNA, separating it by gel electrophoresis, transferring to a membrane, and hybridizing with a labeled Bax-specific probe.

evidence.source-text: This is a standard approach for detecting Bax mRNA expression. RNA is isolated from tissues or cells, separated by size using gel electrophoresis, transferred to a membrane, and hybridised with a labelled Bax-specific probe. The signal indicates both the existence and size of the Bax transcripts (9).

method.description: Measures Bax mRNA expression levels by RNA extraction, reverse transcription to cDNA, and amplification using gene-specific primers with fluorescent dyes or probes for real-time quantification.

evidence.source-text: Used to measure Bax mRNA expression levels, this method involves RNA extraction, reverse transcription to cDNA, and amplification using gene-specific primers. Fluorescent dyes or probes (e.g., SYBR Green, TaqMan) help quantify Bax mRNA in real-time, making it a sensitive method for gene expression analysis (6,7).

method.description: Detects apoptotic DNA fragmentation, often correlated with Bax activation, using labeled nucleotides to identify DNA strand breaks in situ.

evidence.source-text: While not directly measuring Bax, the TUNEL assay detects apoptotic DNA fragmentation, often correlated with Bax activation. It is used in ovarian apoptosis studies alongside Bax expression analysis(4,10).

method.description: Quantifies BDNF exon-specific mRNA expression in hippocampal neuronal cultures using TaqMan-based qRT-PCR, normalized to actin.

evidence.source-text: BDNF quantitative real-time PCR. Hippocampal neuronal cultures were exposed to normal bath solution or 1.0 or 2.0μM Pb2+ for 5 days, and subsequently RNA was harvested according to manufacturer’s instructions (RNeasy; Qiagen), quantified by reading the absorbance at 260 nm, and converted to complementary DNA (cDNA) using 1 μg RNA according to manufacturer’s instructions (High Capacity Reverse Transcription Kit 4368814; Applied Biosystems). Quantitative real-time PCR (q-rtPCR) was performed in triplicate using TaqMan Gene Expression Assays (Applied Biosystems) with 50 ng cDNA using the following probes: Actin (Rat, Rn00667869_m1; Applied Biosystems) and BDNF exon I, exon II, exon IV, and exon IX (Applied Biosystems).

method.description: BDNF protein levels are quantified in cell culture media using a sandwich ELISA. BDNF content is normalized to total protein content.

evidence.source-text: BDNF release via ELISA. Sandwich ELISAs were performed on DIV12 cell culture media using the BDNF Emax ImmunoAssay System kit (Promega, Madison, WI) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
BDNF protein content was divided by total protein for each sample to determine the number of picograms of peptide per microgram of total protein (Stansfield and others 2012).

These assays typically employ either MCT8-transfected Madin-Darby canine kidney (MDCK-1) cells (Braun et al., 2012; Braun & Schweizer, 2015; Johannes et al., 2016; Kinne et al., 2010; Kinne et al., 2009; Roth et al., 2010; Wirth et al., 2009) or MCT8-transfected Human Placenta Choriocarcinoma (JEG3) and African green monkey kidney fibroblast-like cells (COS1) cells (Chen et al., 2022; Groeneweg et al., 2013; Ianculescu et al., 2010).

method.description: T/B-cell cooperation is assessed by measuring murine IL-2 secretion, a marker of T cell activation, using ELISA. ELISA is also used to quantify cytokines in biopsies.

Additional Applications of ELISA: ELISA is also used to quantify cytokines in biopsies, providing insights into immune responses (Nilsen et al., 1998).

evidence.source-text: Histological examination of the reproductive organs

The minimal requirement for estrous staging evaluation by histology is the complete longitudinal sections of the vagina and cervix, transverse sections of the mid-portion of both uterine horns, and middle sections of both ovaries

Persistent estrous is characterized in ovary by the presence of numbers of ovarian follicular cysts (due to pre-ovulatory follicles losing the capacity to ovulate) absence of basophilic corpora lutea and decreased corpora lutea while uterine epithelium becomes tall columnar and vagina may show cornification

method.description: Microscopic examination of longitudinal sections of the vagina, cervix, uterine horns, and ovaries to assess estrous staging and reproductive health.

evidence.source-text: The minimal requirement for estrous staging evaluation by histology is the complete longitudinal sections of the vagina and cervix, transverse sections of the mid-portion of both uterine horns, and middle sections of both ovaries (Goldman 2007; Byers, 2012).

Persistent estrous is characterized in ovary by the presence of numbers of ovarian follicular cysts (due to pre-ovulatory follicles losing the capacity to ovulate) absence of basophilic corpora lutea and decreased corpora lutea while uterine epithelium becomes tall columnar and vagina may show cornification (Westwood, 2008, Dixon, 2014, Shirai 2017, see also Fig. 16).

method.description: Estrous cycle is monitored by observing changes in vaginal smear cytology, looking for cornified epithelial cells. It is non-invasive and inexpensive.

evidence.source-text: Estrous cycle can be monitored in the rat and mouse by observing the changes in the vaginal smear cytology.
It seems to be the most common technique used to determine the phases of the estrous cycle.
The estrous phase shows abundant non-nucleate cornified epithelial cells.

method.description: Observation of changes in vaginal smear cytology to determine the phases of the estrous cycle in rodents. The estrous phase shows abundant non-nucleate cornified epithelial cells with granular cytoplasm and irregular cell shape. Persistent estrous is characterized by cornified vaginal smears for 10 or more days.
method.guideline: OECD TG 421, OECD TG 422, OECD TG 416, OECD TG 443, USA EPA OCSPP 890.1450

evidence.source-text: The estrous phase shows abundant non-nucleate cornified epithelial cells. The cytoplasm is granular, and the cells are irregular in shape. Persistent estrous is characterized by cornified vaginal smears for 10 or more days.

Monitoring of estrous cyclicity is included in OECD test guidelines (TG 421: Reproduction/Developmental Toxicity Screening Test, 2016; TG 422 Combined Repeated Dose Toxicity Study with the Reproduction/Developmental Toxicity Screening Test, 2016; TG 416: Two-Generation Reproduction Toxicity, 2001; TG 443: Extended One-Generation Reproductive Toxicity Study, 2018; and in USA EPA OCSPP 890.1450. Pubertal Development and Thyroid Function in Intact Juvenile/Peripubertal Female Rats Assay, 2011.
Vaginal smear at necropsy is also required in OECD TG 408, OECD TG 421, OECD TG 422 while it is optional in OECD TG 407.

method.description: Fluorescence measurements are used as indirect indicators of QB-site occupation, detecting changes in fluorescence yield and PSII photochemical efficiency due to disrupted electron transfer.

evidence.source-text: Fluorescence-based techniques, including chlorophyll a fluorescence measurements, are frequently applied as indirect but sensitive indicators of QB-site occupation. Inhibitor binding disrupts electron transfer from QA to QB, leading to characteristic changes in fluorescence yield and PSII photochemical efficiency (Sundby, Chow and Anderson, 1993; Maxwell and Johnson, 2000).

evidence.source-text: Resistance mutant analyses, based on naturally occurring or experimentally induced mutations in the psbA gene encoding the D1 protein, offer strong mechanistic evidence for QB-site binding. Altered sensitivity to PSII inhibitors in mutants affecting key QB-site residues (e.g. Ser-264/268) directly links chemical binding to functional inhibition and photosynthetic impairment (Sundby, Chow and Anderson, 1993; Alfonso et al., 1996; Oettmeier, 1999).

method.description: Spectrophotometry monitors changes in absorbance associated with the generation and stabilization of semiquinone radicals, allowing detection and quantification of radical intermediates.
method.measured-endpoint: absorbance changes indicative of semiquinone radical formation

evidence.source-text: The detection of radical formation within redox cyclers by spectrophotometry relies on the ability to monitor changes in absorbance associated with the generation and stabilization of specific radical intermediates, most commonly semiquinone radicals.

By recording the absorption spectrum during redox cycling under anaerobic or low-oxygen conditions (to prevent rapid reoxidation), the formation of the radical intermediate can be detected in real time.

method.description: The Amplex Red Ultra assay quantitatively measures hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) using a horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-catalyzed reaction that produces the fluorescent compound resorufin, allowing real-time monitoring of mitochondrial ROS production.

evidence.source-text: The Amplex® Red Ultra assay has emerged as a sensitive and specific technique for the quantitative measurement of hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), a primary and relatively stable ROS generated by mitochondria (Grivennikova et al. 2018).
The fluorescence intensity of resorufin is directly proportional to the amount of H₂O₂ present, allowing real-time monitoring of mitochondrial ROS production.
To perform the assay, isolated mitochondria or permeabilized cells are incubated in a reaction buffer containing Amplex Red Ultra, HRP, and appropriate mitochondrial substrates and inhibitors.

method.description: A non-invasive method using coelenterazine derivatives that undergo oxidative decarboxylation in the presence of ROS to emit blue light.

evidence.source-text: Coelenterazine chemiluminescence is a sensitive and non-invasive analytical method for detecting elevated mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), particularly superoxide (O₂•⁻) and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), in intact cells and isolated mitochondria

The intensity of this light emission is directly proportional to the amount of ROS present, enabling real-time quantification of oxidative stress under physiological and pathophysiological conditions.
Coelenterazine chemiluminescence is particularly suited for high-throughput screening and longitudinal studies

method.description: This assay detects elevated mitochondrial ROS (superoxide and hydrogen peroxide) using coelenterazine, a luminescent substrate that emits photons upon reaction with ROS. The intensity of light emission is proportional to ROS amount.

evidence.source-text: Coelenterazine chemiluminescence is a sensitive and non-invasive analytical method for detecting elevated mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), particularly superoxide (O₂•⁻) and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), in intact cells and isolated mitochondria (Lucas et al. 1992; Teranishi et al. 1997).

The intensity of this light emission is directly proportional to the amount of ROS present, enabling real-time quantification of oxidative stress under physiological and pathophysiological conditions.

Unlike fluorescence-based ROS probes, which often require excitation light that may introduce phototoxicity or interfere with mitochondrial function, chemiluminescence avoids exogenous illumination and thereby minimizes assay artifacts.

The intensity of this light emission is directly proportional to the amount of ROS present, enabling real-time quantification of oxidative stress under physiological and pathophysiological conditions.
In experimental applications, cells or mitochondria are incubated with coelenterazine under controlled metabolic conditions.

method.description: Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectroscopy directly detects unpaired electrons in paramagnetic species, such as mitochondrial ROS, using spin-trapping agents to stabilize and identify specific radical species.

evidence.source-text: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, also known as electron spin resonance (ESR), is a powerful and direct analytical technique for the detection of unpaired electrons in paramagnetic species, including free radicals such as reactive oxygen species (ROS).

Native ROS such as superoxide (O₂•⁻), hydroxyl radicals (•OH), and nitric oxide (NO•) are typically too reactive and short-lived to be measured directly by EPR. Therefore, EPR detection of mitochondrial ROS relies primarily on the use of spin-trapping agents (Griendling et al. 2016).

To measure mitochondrial ROS formation using EPR, isolated mitochondria or permeabilized cells are incubated with suitable substrates and respiratory chain inhibitors in the presence of the spin trap.

method.description: MitoSOX is a fluorogenic probe that selectively detects mitochondrial superoxide in live cells by oxidizing to a fluorescent product that binds to mitochondrial DNA.

evidence.source-text: MitoSOX™ dyes are a family of fluorogenic probes specifically designed for the selective detection of mitochondrial superoxide in live cells.

Upon entry into the mitochondria, MitoSOX Red is oxidized specifically by superoxide to form a highly fluorescent ethidium-like product that binds to mitochondrial DNA, emitting red fluorescence upon excitation.
In practical applications, live cells or isolated mitochondria are incubated with MitoSOX Red under controlled conditions, typically at concentrations of 2–5 μM for 10–30 minutes at 37°C.

method.description: Quantifies estradiol levels in ovarian tissue using antibody-based detection methods, typically ELISA, which is the preferred technique for measuring hormone concentrations.

evidence.source-text: Estradiol can be measured via immunoassay, mass spectrometry or Western blotting, with immunoassay the preferred technique (for review of techniques see Rosner et al. 2013).

Studies that utilized immunoassay include (Sashida and Johnson 1976; Spears et al. 1998; Li et al. 2008; Murray et al. 2008; Gan et al. 2024), and include commercially available ELISA kits (e.g. Neogen 402110; ALPCO 11-ESTHU-E01; Cayman Chemical 501890).

method.description: Quantifies transcription of the aromatase gene (cyp19) via quantitative real-time PCR, providing a semi-quantitative indicator of potential estradiol synthesis.

evidence.source-text: Since estradiol is generally synthesized from other steroids, real time PCR is generally not used, but transcription of key steroid biosynthesis genes, particularly cyp19 (aromatase) would be an indirect – and only semi-quantitative indicator of potential changes in estradiol hormone levels.

Enzymes involved in steroid biosynthesis in the ovaries can also be studied via immunoassay, Western blotting, or real time PCR (studies that utilized this approach include Li et al. 2008; Gan et al. 2024).
